stage: Stages 1-2: object perception and tracking, camera ego-motion, table plane, hands. Verdict: these stages put off-the-shelf foundation models together with standard geometric glue. After a real search, I found no novel component. The closest whole-pipeline prior art (EgoXperience's EgoX-Engine, Oct 2026; HO-Cap, 2024) has nearly the same architecture, and it adds two things we lack: tracking verification and recovery, and hand keypoints triangulated across views. Two corrections to the brief, from reading the code. (1) The object detector is not OWLv2. OWLv2 was dropped on 2026-10-13: the docstring of /home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/perc2.py is stale and its PROMPT dict is unused. (2) The hand lift is a similarity fit of MediaPipe's own 3-D hand shape to the stereo depth, not a per-keypoint depth lookup. The dataset has no hand ground truth, so no hand-accuracy number exists. Every prior-art item marked 'verified' was opened: arXiv abstract or HTML fetched with curl, since WebFetch could not resolve arxiv.org. Items marked 'not opened' come from search snippets or from the repo's own notes.

components.component: Stereo depth
components.what_we_do: /home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/perc2.py L52-112. The mono pair is rectified with cv2.stereoRectify (left = ego_cam_c, right = ego_cam_b, 1600x1000). The released FoundationStereo ViT-L checkpoint (23-51-11) runs unchanged at 0.5x scale with 32 iterations and AMP. The disparity is upsampled, z = f*B/d, and only 0.15-2.0 m is kept. Depth is cached per episode at about 0.27 s/frame. The same depth feeds tracking, camera motion, hand lifting and the TSDF meshes.
components.closest_prior_art: FoundationStereo (Wen et al., CVPR 2025) https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09898 [verified]. HOT3D (Banerjee et al., CVPR 2025) https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19167 [verified HTML]: in-hand object 3-D lifting reaches recall@10 cm of 96.8% with StereoMatch (Quest3, 2 views) vs 30.2% with MonoDepth (Aria), both with GT masks. EgoXperience's EgoX-Engine https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26625 [verified HTML] gets metric depth from a calibrated head-mounted stereo pair. The organiser ships a v2d_foundation_stereo wrapper but its ego baseline uses monocular MoGe (repo note 03; not re-opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Only the choice to use the stereo pair instead of the organiser baseline's monocular depth. That choice is standard for stereo rigs (HOT3D, EgoX-Engine, RGB-D in HO-Cap). There is no fine-tuning, no temporal stereo and no confidence map.
components.evidence_it_matters: No stereo-vs-mono ablation was run in this repo. Indirect: whole perception scores mean AUC 0.932 over 20 public episodes (scan templates, scored vs mocap after inference; work-log 2026-10-20). The external evidence is HOT3D's numbers above.

components.component: Frame-0 object detection and identity assignment
components.what_we_do:
/home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/perc2.py L166-242.
- Proposals: SAM2.1-L automatic mask generator on the grey rectified frame 0 (32 points/side, area >= 400 px).
- Descriptors: DINOv2-L CLS of each masked crop vs grey nvdiffrast renders of each mesh from 42 icosphere views.
- Score: mean of the top-5 cosine similarities - 0.3*|mean-intensity difference|/255. Gated to proposals whose stereo 3-D PCA extent (3-97 pct) is 0.3-1.3x the mesh's largest OBB extent.
- Assignment (default DET_PRIOR=compact): a brute-force joint choice over each object's top-80 proposals minimising -sum(S) + 0.5*max(0, max pairwise 3-D centroid distance - 0.45 m); Hungarian otherwise.
- /home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/perc.py ('perc4'; not the default, unvalidated) adds render-and-compare verification: FoundationPose register on each object's top-4 proposals, scored by depth agreement matched/(matched + free-space violations).
components.closest_prior_art: CNOS (Nguyen et al., ICCVW 2023) https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.11067 [verified HTML: SAM proposals, 42 icosphere templates, DINOv2 CLS matching]. SAM-6D ISM (Lin et al., CVPR 2024) https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.15707 [verified HTML: top-K-averaged semantic score + appearance score + geometric score = box IoU of a depth-located coarse pose]. Detection verification: EgoX-Engine checks the posed model against observed depth (verified); EgoGrasp filters frames by IoU between the SAM2 mask and the projected mesh, https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01050 [verified HTML]. The compactness term is a hand-written scene-context prior; context priors in detection are classic, but no specific paper was opened.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Grey templates for a monochrome camera; a 3-D size gate from stereo in place of SAM-6D's 2-D box IoU; an episode-level co-location prior over the joint assignment. These are small dataset-specific changes, and the core is CNOS.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured on public episodes (scored after inference). OWLv2 on grey frames failed on ep0/2/18/21 and swapped ep11's twin cups (AUC 0.10); the CNOS-style detector gives ep11 0.871. The compact prior raised the 20-episode mean from 0.883 to 0.932 (ep26 0.065 -> 0.988; work-log 2026-10-20). perc.py's verification has no validated number.

components.component: Object 6-DoF registration and tracking
components.what_we_do:
/home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/perc2.py L149-255.
- Released FoundationPose, model-based, one estimator per object, using our own meshes (MESH_DIR; only our meshes on eval episodes) with vertex colours turned grey.
- register(iteration=5) on frame 0 with the chosen mask, then track_one(iteration=2) on every later frame from the previous pose.
- Objects are tracked independently. After frame 0 there are no masks, no hand masking, no failure detection or re-registration, no symmetry handling and no temporal smoothing.
- Output: cam_T_obj per frame, composed with world_T_cam.
components.closest_prior_art:
FoundationPose (Wen et al., CVPR 2024) https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08344 [verified].
- The same chain (calibrated stereo depth + scanned-model init + FoundationPose tracking) appears in EgoXperience's EgoX-Engine https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26625 [verified HTML], which adds depth-agreement verification and SLAM world alignment.
- HO-Cap https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06843 [verified HTML]: multi-view FoundationPose re-seeded from fused poses, plus SDF refinement with a smoothness term.
- Trackers with loss detection and recovery: Woven/Bonn https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23468 [verified abstract], STORM https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.09771 [verified abstract], SuperPose https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19986 [verified abstract], RGBTrack https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17119 [verified abstract], FoundationPose++ (github teal024/FoundationPose-plus-plus: 2D tracker + Kalman filter; search snippet only, not opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing in the tracker; grey textures are the only adaptation. Re-tracking with meshes fused along our own tracks (track -> fuse -> re-track) belongs to stage 3, and BundleSDF/HO-Cap-style pipelines also do it.
components.evidence_it_matters:
Measured on public episodes: mean AUC 0.932 with scan templates. Weak episodes:
- ep0 0.18: lid registered 179 deg off by symmetry; the pot track jumps ~10 cm at f75 while it is static in GT.
- ep24 0.85, ep11 0.87, ep31 0.89.

With our meshes: ep18 0.970 (scan 0.957); ep24 0.795 (wooden_piece_1 0.76).

components.component: Camera ego-motion
components.what_we_do:
/home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/perc2.py L114-147.
- SIFT (4000 features) on every rectified-left frame; Lowe ratio 0.75 from keyframe to frame.
- Keyframe keypoints are back-projected with the keyframe's stereo depth, then solvePnPRansac (SQPnP, 1.5 px, 2000 iterations, >= 20 inliers) and LM refinement.
- A new keyframe starts when inliers fall below KF_MIN (120 from pipeline_ep.sh). On failure the previous pose is held. World = rectified-left camera at frame 0.
- There is no hand/object masking, no bundle adjustment and no loop closure. perc.py (not the default) masks rendered objects and prefers frame 0 or recent keyframes.
components.closest_prior_art: Frame-to-keyframe stereo/RGB-D PnP tracking as in ORB-SLAM2's tracking thread (Mur-Artal & Tardos 2017) https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.06475 [verified abstract], here without its local map, BA or loop closure. HaWoR's hand-masked adaptive SLAM https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02973 [verified abstract]. The organiser baseline uses monocular DROID-SLAM (repo note 03). Map relocalisation: HLoc (Sarlin et al. 2019) https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.03506 [verified abstract].
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing beyond textbook; it is simpler than ORB-SLAM2 stereo.
components.evidence_it_matters: No direct GT camera error is logged for perc2. Pot-only public episodes chain 105-194 keyframes; drift was suspected (work-log 2026-10-13). Repo note 18 measured a factory-extrinsic stereo VO drifting 20-83 mm on 12/20 eval clips and modelled +0.10 AUC from a room map. That is an estimate, not an end-to-end run, and I did not verify that it was this exact VO.

components.component: Table plane, gravity and table extent
components.what_we_do:
/home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/mkref.py fit_table (L335-410) and table_disc (L443).
- Sequential RANSAC (up to 4 planes, 6 mm threshold) on frame-0 stereo points in a ring around the objects' projected footprints.
- Support plane = parallel to the dominant plane (within 25 deg) and closest under the lowest object point. Table frame: z = normal, origin under the objects' centroid.
- Real table disc = minimum enclosing circle of the connected on-plane region.
- /home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/recon_mesh.py re-fits the plane per frame (corrections up to 10 deg).
components.closest_prior_art: RANSAC support-plane / tabletop segmentation (Fischler & Bolles 1981; the Rusu/PCL tabletop pipeline) [not opened]. The organiser baseline takes gravity from GeoCalib (repo note 03).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: The rule 'the plane closest under the objects' (so the floor does not win) is a sensible heuristic, not a method.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured bugs, now fixed: plain RANSAC chose the floor 60 cm down on ep12; the real table radius is 0.22-0.25 m, not the 0.45 m sim default, so the table edges used in ep24 and ep18 were missing in the simulation.

components.component: 2-D hand keypoints
components.what_we_do:
/home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/hands_mp.py L281-319, L509-530.
- MediaPipe Hands, legacy API: model_complexity 1, tracking mode, up to 2 hands, detection/tracking confidence 0.3.
- Runs on the colour cam_a video (stereo frame k pairs with colour frame k+1). Output: 21 image landmarks, 21 metric 'world' landmarks and a handedness label.
- The colour camera is used because the mono rectified cameras gave about 0 frames with both hands detected.
components.closest_prior_art: MediaPipe Hands (Zhang et al. 2020) https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.10214 [verified abstract]. Used the same way in HO-Cap (verified HTML) and AnyTeleop https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04577 [verified HTML]. The stronger models the organiser baseline uses: HaMeR https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.05251 and WiLoR https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12259 [both verified abstracts].
components.what_is_genuinely_different: None. The choice follows from the MANO licence (MANO_RIGHT.pkl was not obtained).
components.evidence_it_matters: Detection: ep12 173/181 frames, ep0 338/373. It misses hands in fast motion (ep18 right hand, f18-22) and out of view (ep24 right hand, f0-16). On ep24 the 2-D landmarks sit on the hands even where the 3-D lift fails.

components.component: 3-D hand lifting with stereo depth
components.what_we_do:
/home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/hands_mp.py L140-277, L585-601.
- Depth: rectified-left stereo depth is back-projected (stride 2), moved rect -> c -> b -> a with factory extrinsics, and min-z-buffered into a half-resolution cam_a depth map.
- Per landmark: samples in a 7x7 window, keep those within 3 cm of the 10th percentile, take the median, add an 8 mm skin-to-joint offset; reject values > 15 cm from the hand median.
- Fit: MediaPipe's world-landmark shape as a similarity (R, t, scale clamped to 0.85-1.15) to all 21 reprojections (sigma 4 px) plus the depth residuals (sigma 12 mm), Huber loss. Initialised by SQPnP and 4-point RANSAC-Umeyama.
- Automatic mirror check of the world landmarks; fits with rms > 20 px are rejected; the result goes to world with world_T_cam.
components.closest_prior_art:
- AnyTeleop [verified HTML]: MediaPipe keypoints + per-keypoint depth lookup + PnP for the wrist pose.
- Organiser baseline align_hands: translation-only shift of MANO to MoGe depth on hand-minus-object pixels (repo note 01; not re-opened).
- HO-Cap [verified HTML]: MediaPipe in 8 RGB-D views, pairwise triangulation, MANO fit with per-subject shape.
- EgoXperience [verified HTML]: hand keypoints by cross-view triangulation from head stereo.
- STB stereo hand benchmark https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.07214 [verified abstract].
components.what_is_genuinely_different: A rigid-plus-scale fit of MediaPipe's own 3-D shape, jointly to reprojection and robust cross-camera stereo depth. AnyTeleop runs PnP on per-keypoint depth; HO-Cap and EgoXperience triangulate. Good engineering, not a new method. It takes keypoints from one view and uses the stereo pair only as a depth map.
components.evidence_it_matters: No hand GT exists. ep12: median scale 0.839 (wrist to middle tip 11.9 cm) even with relaxed bounds; small hand vs depth bias is unresolved. ep24: during the grip the stereo depth at hand pixels lands on the board, the scale sits on its clamp, robot targets end up inside the board, and the wrist IK error reaches 17-20 cm.

components.component: Hand identity, temporal linking and gap filling
components.what_we_do:
/home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/hands_mp.py L322-486, L532-553.
- Left/right swap is decided by the image x-position of the two labels over two-hand frames, with the chirality median as tie-break.
- Default greedy linker by palm-centroid distance: duplicates < 3 cm removed, 10 cm swap margin, reassignment, 25 cm jump gate.
- Optional Viterbi over per-frame assignments with label, forearm, image-side and motion costs.
- Outlier rejection (> 6 cm from the local median), linear fill of gaps up to 15 frames, Savitzky-Golay smoothing (window 7, order 2), hold elsewhere.
components.closest_prior_art: Tracking-by-detection with nearest-neighbour/Hungarian association and HMM/Viterbi identity decoding (multi-object tracking textbook practice; not opened). Learned infilling: HaWoR's motion infiller and Dyn-HaMR's interacting-hand prior https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.12861 [both verified abstracts].
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing of substance. Learned infilling (HaWoR) is stronger than linear interpolation plus hold.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured A/B (proxy: human palm steps > 4 cm; no GT): greedy best or tied on ep31/39/22/18/24; Viterbi fixed only the ep12 hand-over. Holding the first seen pose back to frame 0 made the robot hands overlap on ep24. mkref's lead-in plus 4 cm hand separation moved ep24 end to end from 0.080 to 0.232 (one seed).

components.component: Bone-length-consistent hand refinement
components.what_we_do:
/home/user/v2d-track3/pipeline/hand_refine.py.
- Per hand: reference bone lengths = per-bone medians over the best 30% of frames (measured, depth found, lowest reprojection rms). Reference palm (wrist, thumb CMC, 4 MCPs) = Procrustes median.
- Per frame: rigid palm fit, then each finger joint is placed on the camera ray of its 2-D landmark at the current length clipped to +-10% of the reference.
- Of the two ray-sphere roots, the one nearer MediaPipe's prediction wins; if the ray misses, the nearest sphere point is used.
- Savitzky-Golay smoothing, then lengths re-clipped.
components.closest_prior_art: Closed-form ray/bone-length lifting: Taylor, CVIU 2000 [not opened]; KITRO https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19833 [verified abstract: bone directions in closed form from 2-D pose, bone length and parent joint]; Kaeser-Chen & Guleryuz, ICIP 2018 'Fast lifting' [search snippet only]. Per-subject shape calibration: HO-Cap pre-calibrates MANO shape per subject [verified]; Dyn-HaMR and HOLD share shape over a sequence.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Applied to MediaPipe skeletons with an episode-level, data-selected bone template and a +-10% margin instead of MANO beta. The two-root ambiguity is broken by the network's own 3-D prediction.
components.evidence_it_matters: ep24 bone-length CV 0.24 -> 0.07 (left) and 0.22 -> 0.08 (right); flexion-invariant chain ratio p10 0.85 -> 0.98. Its effect on the sim score was never isolated (no A/B).

components.component: Stages 1-2 as a whole
components.what_we_do: Objects: stereo depth -> CNOS-style frame-0 identification with a size gate and co-location prior -> per-object FoundationPose tracking with our meshes -> keyframe SIFT+PnP camera motion -> RANSAC table plane. Hands: MediaPipe on the colour camera -> stereo-depth similarity lift -> greedy linking and filling -> bone-length refinement. Ground truth is read only by scoring.
components.closest_prior_art:
- EgoXperience's EgoX-Engine (2026-10-19) https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26625 [verified HTML]: calibrated head-mounted stereo depth + SLAM session frame + SAM 3 masks + pre-scanned model pose initialised with stereo depth + FoundationPose tracking + depth-agreement verification + hand keypoints by cross-view triangulation. Essentially our architecture.
- HO-Cap (2024) [verified HTML]: MediaPipe + SAM2 + FoundationPose + BundleSDF meshes + SDF refinement.
- RoboWheel (repo's competitor note; not re-opened): HaMeR + UniDepth + Hunyuan3D mesh + FoundationPose + DROID-SLAM.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Dataset-specific choices: stereo instead of the baseline's monocular MoGe, the colour camera for hands, our own fused meshes as templates. They help against the organiser's chain but follow a design others have published. Compared with EgoX-Engine and HO-Cap we lack tracking verification/recovery and multi-view hand triangulation.
components.evidence_it_matters: Perception is not the main loss on hard episodes: our references score 0.98 (ep18) and 0.80-0.82 (ep24) vs mocap while policies score 0.31-0.40 (forensics 2026-10-21; overnight 2026-10-22). The remaining perception losses are concentrated in a few episodes (ep0 0.18; ep24 0.80-0.85).

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Rest detection in the style of a zero-velocity update. A resting object counts as static until a hand touches it. When no lifted hand joint is within ~3 cm of an object and FoundationPose's frame-to-frame motion stays under a threshold, freeze the object at one robust pose (SE(3) median of the best-verified frames in the interval), ignore further tracker updates, and re-register when a hand arrives.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Pedestrian inertial navigation: Foxlin 2005, 'Pedestrian tracking with shoe-mounted inertial sensors', IEEE CG&A [secondary sources only]; review by Wahlstrom & Skog, https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09208 [search result, not opened]. EgoGrasp anchors motion to the static world to suppress noise [verified HTML].
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Our tracker has no notion of rest, so resting objects drift and jump. ep0's pot jumps ~10 cm at f75 while static in GT. A wrong slot-0 anchor pose shifts the scorer's single alignment for the whole episode, and resting objects floating 1-4 cm in our references hurt the simulation.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 1 day, CPU only, on the cached poses and hands. Risk: a slow push or slide (the ep24 board slide f8-15) mislabelled as rest; mitigate with a depth-residual check before freezing.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Re-score the 20 public episodes vs mocap after inference with the rest prior on and off. Falsified if the mean AUC gain is below 0.005, ep0's pot AUC does not rise, or any episode drops more than 0.01.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Multi-hypothesis trajectory decoding. Keep K pose hypotheses per object per frame: FoundationPose register outputs including symmetric flips, forward and backward tracks, and re-registrations triggered by a failing depth-agreement check. Score each by render-and-compare depth agreement (the verify() already written in perc.py) and choose one globally consistent trajectory with Viterbi using motion smoothness and the rest prior.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Hand2Robot https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15769 [verified abstract]: picks a globally consistent trajectory from per-frame pose candidates using confidence plus temporal constraints. Multiple-hypothesis tracking (Reid 1979, radar) [not opened]. Recovery trackers: STORM https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.09771 and Woven/Bonn https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23468 [verified abstracts].
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: FoundationPose commits to one pose per frame and never recovers. The worst perception losses are near-ties and lost tracks: ep0 lid 179 deg off (episode AUC 0.18), 180-deg board and sweeper near-ties, ep24 wooden_piece_1 0.76.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-3 days. Extra GPU time for re-registration, roughly 5-20 min per episode (estimate). Risk: the depth-agreement score cannot separate exact symmetries (lid), so colour or marker evidence would still be needed there.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On the 20 public episodes, compare perception AUC vs mocap after inference. Falsified if ep0 stays below 0.5 and the mean gain is under 0.01.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Forward-backward tracking with a consistency check. Also track every object backward from the last frame, where objects usually rest and are clearly visible after placement. Per frame, keep the direction whose pose has the better depth/silhouette agreement, and flag frames where the two directions disagree as unreliable.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Forward-backward error in TLD (Kalal et al. 2010) [not opened]; Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoothing (estimation theory). The organiser's SAM2 stage already propagates masks in reverse, then forward (repo note 01).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Errors accumulate in one direction: re-grasps, occlusions and flips corrupt everything after them. A backward pass rebuilds the second half from a clean start at almost no engineering cost.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 1 day; twice the tracking time (seconds to minutes per episode). Risk: the end state can also be occluded (an object in a rack or under a lid).
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Public episodes, per-frame error vs mocap after inference. Falsified if the merged track does not beat the forward track's mean AUC by at least 0.005, or if the agreement flag does not concentrate the large-error frames (precision < 0.5).

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Ground-truth-free persistent room map. The head rig records in the same room in every episode. Build one SfM map from public (and optionally eval) video frames, make it metric with the stereo baseline, take gravity from the table plane, and relocalise every frame against it instead of chaining keyframes. This must not reuse note 18's mocap registration: that registration is derived from GT, and the scorer's first-pose alignment does not need it.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: HLoc https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.03506 [verified abstract]. ORB-SLAM2's map reuse and localization mode https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.06475 [verified abstract]. AR 'cloud anchors' / lifelong localisation. The repo's own note 18 prototype (pycolmap, 21.5 min CPU map, 100% coverage of the 20 eval clips).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The keyframe chain drifts, and there is no BA or loop closure. Note 18 measured relocalised poses within ~2 mm / 0.03 deg of bundle-adjusted poses and modelled +0.10 AUC against a stereo VO drifting 20-83 mm (an estimate).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 1-2 days CPU integration. Risks: rare single-keyframe glitches of 7-11 mm (note 18; a VO consistency gate catches them); the map must be rebuilt for each episode left out when validating; a large occluder covering >= 75% of the image width degrades the pose.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On the 20 public episodes, use maps that exclude each test episode's frames, swap only world_T_cam, and re-score perception vs mocap after inference. Falsified if the mean gain is below 0.01 and the pot-only episodes 41-45 do not improve.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Physics-consistent multi-object projection. After tracking, solve for object trajectories that stay close to the FoundationPose poses but show no penetration between objects or with the table, and rest on a support when untouched. Use the simulator's own collision, as contact_retarget.py already does for hands. In effect this is data assimilation of a rigid-body model to noisy pose observations.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: PhysPose https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23587 [verified abstract]: non-penetration and gravity post-optimisation for single images. Grasp-and-Lift https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18121 [verified abstract]: CMA-ES with the physics engine as a black box. 4D-Var data assimilation in weather forecasting (analogy).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Objects are tracked independently and not checked against physics. Measured: objects float 1-4 cm above the table in our ep12, ep24 and ep27 references; ep26 has a pot inside a rack and ep2 a lid on a pot. Fixing this at the source also feeds better references to stage 4.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-3 days CPU. It overlaps with the stage-4 rest_settle. Risk: wrong contact states push objects off a correct perceived pose, which can lower AUC.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Perception AUC vs mocap on the 20 public episodes, plus float and penetration statistics. Falsified if the AUC change is below +0.005 or negative, or if sim_vs_ref of retrained ep12 and ep27 policies does not improve.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Triangulate hand keypoints across the colour camera and the mono pair instead of reading surface depth. Match each cam_a landmark into the rectified mono views along epipolar lines with DINOv2 patch features, or run a 2-D hand keypoint model on mono crops located from the cam_a box. Triangulate with the factory calibration, keep MediaPipe's shape as a prior, and refit.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: HO-Cap [verified HTML]: MediaPipe per view plus pairwise triangulation. EgoXperience [verified HTML]: cross-view keypoint triangulation from head stereo. HOT3D [verified HTML]: two-view UmeTrack 10.9 vs single-view 15.4 mm MKPE on HOT3D, and in-hand lifting by stereo matching of DINOv2 features. UmeTrack https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00099 [verified abstract]: multi-view mono VR hand tracking.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Our lift reads the depth of whatever surface is in front of the joint. When a hand grips, that is the object (ep24: hand squashed into the board, scale on the clamp, robot targets inside the board). Triangulated keypoints do not depend on that surface, and they would also show whether the 0.84 hand scale is a depth bias.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-3 days. Risks: MediaPipe failed on mono frames, so matching quality on grey 1280x800 images is unknown; the colour-mono baseline is short; joints hidden in all views stay unobserved.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: No hand GT exists, so use GT-free proxies on ep24, ep18 and ep12: reprojection error in a held-out view, bone-length CV, share of joints inside tracked object meshes, and robot wrist-IK p95; then sim AUC on ep24. Falsified if joints-inside-object frames on ep24 do not drop by at least 30%.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Cheapest test of the same mechanism: object-aware depth sampling for the hand lift. Drop depth samples that fall on the tracked objects' rendered silhouettes (we have the poses and meshes) and sample only inside SAM2 hand masks prompted by the MediaPipe points.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: The organiser baseline aligns hands on hand-mask-minus-object-mask pixels (repo note 01, not re-opened). HO-Cap and BundleSDF use per-frame masks.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: sample_zbuf takes the nearest surface within 3 cm of the 10th percentile. That is the object whenever it lies between the camera and a fingertip, which is exactly the ep24 failure.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About half a day; one GPU pass for the renders and SAM2. Risk: few depth samples remain for fingers wrapped behind an object, so the fit falls back to MediaPipe's shape.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep24 and ep18: collapsed-frame share, chain-ratio p10, and joints-inside-object fraction before vs after. Falsified if none improves by at least 20% relative.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Per-clip temporal calibration between the colour and mono streams. hands_mp.py pairs stereo frame k with colour frame k+1 everywhere. Estimate a fractional, possibly piecewise lag per clip by maximising agreement between the lifted hand (or SIFT-tracked static scene points) reprojected across cameras, and interpolate.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Kalibr's unified temporal and spatial calibration (Furgale et al., IROS 2013) [not opened]; time-offset estimation in visual-inertial odometry. Repo note 18 measured GT-free lags of -1.05..-1.20 frames, and eval clip 20 switching to -2.1 at frame 50.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: A one-frame error at a 0.6 m/s reach (ep18) is ~3 cm of hand position, so it directly produces depth-reprojection conflicts and IK target errors.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 1 day CPU. Risk: small gain on slow episodes; a jump in the lag inside a clip needs change-point handling.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Sweep the lag on public episodes. Falsified if the fitted lag does not reduce median dz_med and palm jitter vs the fixed offset, or does not reproduce note 18's per-clip lags within 0.2 frames.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Use the visible mocap marker spheres as natural fiducials. Detect the bright spheres in the stereo images, triangulate them, estimate their positions in the object frame along our own tracks (from our reconstructions, not the public scans, to stay within the own-meshes rule), and use them to break symmetric spins and correct drift.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Fiducial-marker tracking (AprilTag/ArUco); optical motion capture itself. The repo's note 17 prototype: a marker-only lid tracker reached AUC 0.977 with full fixes in 98-100% of frames, but it is not viable as the primary tracker for cups or the pot (markers are lost in grasps).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Shape cannot disambiguate the lid's 180-deg spin (ep0 0.18) or cup spins, and the markers can. They are physically present in the eval videos, so this reads no ground truth.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-4 days. Rule risk: confirm that using markers visible in the video is acceptable (the Kaggle rule bans hand labelling, not image cues). Technical risk: few markers visible during grasps (note 17).
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep0 and the lid/cup public episodes: perception AUC after inference with marker spin correction vs without. Falsified if ep0 does not rise above 0.6.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: A generative joint hand-object motion prior, guided by our observations, to fill in occluded or out-of-view object and hand motion consistently, instead of linear interpolation, hold and independent tracking.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: WHOLE https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22209 [verified abstract]: a learned hand-object motion prior guided at test time to fit egocentric video. EgoGrasp https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01050 [verified HTML]: HOI-prior diffusion that fills in object 6-DoF from reliable frames in wrist coordinates.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Our hands are filled by interpolation and hold, so robot hands appeared from nowhere and overlapped (ep24 f0-16). Objects are tracked without any hand-object coupling. Joint generative reconstruction is reported to beat separate-then-post-process pipelines.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: High: code and weights availability unchecked, MANO dependence (licence not obtained), priors trained on monocular data, and the freeze is on 2026-11-04. The most likely use is an offline diagnostic on the hard episodes, not a pipeline swap.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On ep24, ep0 and ep18, perception AUC vs mocap after inference plus hand-QA proxies. Falsified if neither improves over ours together with the cheaper rest prior and multi-hypothesis ideas.

stage: Stage 3 (+8): own mesh reconstruction (pipeline/recon_mesh.py, mesh_color.py, flatten_base.py, make_assets.py; meshes/library_v1..v4; in-progress interaction census in scratchpad/interact). VERDICT: the implemented parts are standard practice with a few careful adaptations. Their lineage runs from Curless & Levoy 1996 TSDF and space carving through Co-Fusion/MaskFusion per-object fusion to BundleSDF's hybrid free-space SDF, and each adaptation was checked by a measurement. None of it is novel. The organisers already ship two close tools in nvidia-isaac/video_to_data: BundleSDF that builds an SDF from given poses, depth and masks, and a mesh_to_usd drop test with a recorded-support pose. Only the planned interaction-aware step (stage 8: non-penetration of co-located objects across a whole video, fingertips as virtual touch, resting-support patches) reaches 'new combination', and it is not built and has no score yet. Two honest caveats. (1) The library meshes were fused along tracks that FoundationPose produced with the public scans as templates, and in the library build `--others` carved with the scans too (the owner's 'A-lite' decision). So the hard joint tracking-plus-reconstruction problem, BundleSDF's core contribution, has not been solved by us. (2) The largest measured defect is wall thickness and filled cavities, which the code makes structural: 4 mm voxels, 12 mm truncation, and meshing from a blurred binary occupancy instead of the TSDF zero crossing. Preliminary diagnostics from the running workflow (scans used for diagnosis only) show thin parts reconstructed 8–15.5 mm thick where the scans are 1.6–3.5 mm. Volumes are 3.5x the scan for the lid and 4.2x for the pitcher. These are the defects the literature fixes with finer sparse TSDF, shape priors or generative completion. Leaderboard CD-O is 0.065 cm (SoySauceChicken) and 0.313 cm (Zihao Guo); ours is 0.22–1.15 cm on public episodes. These are different episodes, so the comparison is indicative only. Verification note: in this VM WebFetch could not resolve any host, so primary sources were checked with curl. arXiv abstracts came from export.arxiv.org, the BundleSDF and Tzionas-Gall full texts from ar5iv, and READMEs from raw.githubusercontent.com. Items marked 'search snippet only' were not opened.

components.component: 1. Core: object-frame TSDF fusion of stereo depth along our own tracks
components.what_we_do: recon_mesh.py integrate(). A 150^3 grid of 4 mm voxels covers a cube of ±30 cm around the object origin. For every 2nd frame (stride 2 in the library builds) each voxel is projected with cam_T_obj[t] into the rectified-left FoundationStereo depth (1600x1000, K from cv2.stereoRectify). sdf = D(u) - z. Voxels more than 12 mm behind the surface are skipped. All other voxels take an unweighted running mean of clip(sdf/12 mm, -1, 1), so free space (+1) erases anything not rigidly attached. Voxels with fewer than 3 updates count as unknown. An optional 5x5 depth edge filter (max-min > 2 cm) is the default but was turned off for the dust pan. There are no masks, no per-pixel uncertainty weights and no pose refinement. It runs on CPU: 1.5–4 min for one object from one episode, 23–38 min for 3–4 fused episodes (blue cup 1371 s, dust pan 2288 s).
components.closest_prior_art: Curless & Levoy 1996, 'A volumetric method for building complex models from range images' (https://graphics.stanford.edu/papers/volrange/; existence verified via Semantic Scholar metadata, page unreachable from this VM). Co-Fusion (https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06629) and MaskFusion (https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.09194): per-object TSDF in the object frame given per-object tracking (verified, arXiv abstracts). BundleSDF (https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14158; verified, full text opened). The organisers' own v2d_bundlesdf: 'BundleSDF SDF training and texture baking from pre-computed poses, depth, and masks' (https://github.com/nvidia-isaac/video_to_data/tree/main/reconstruction/modules/v2d_bundlesdf; verified, README opened). Weise et al. 2009, 'In-hand scanning with online loop closure' (search snippet only). Competitor tianny0078/v2d-track3 also uses multi-frame TSDF (README opened, verified).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Little. The organisers' module does the same job (SDF from given poses, depth and masks) with a neural SDF. Ours is a dependency-free CPU numpy version fed with FoundationStereo depth on the rectified mono pair, which helps reproducibility and licensing (BundleSDF is non-commercial). It is weaker than standard TSDF practice in three ways: uniform weights instead of depth- or angle-dependent ones, 4 mm voxels with 12 mm truncation (no thin walls), and no joint pose refinement.
components.evidence_it_matters: Registered AUC with our mesh vs with the scan (same tracks): ep41 pot 0.998/0.999 and ep23 boards 0.997/0.999 (v5); ep39 dust pan 0.953/0.997; ep21 cup+pitcher 0.917/0.975; library_v1: ep42 0.958/0.986, ep45 0.964/0.966, ep24 0.864/0.840, ep11 beige cup 0.857/0.914, sweeper ep31 0.801/0.876 with flip rate 0.12–0.25. Tracking with our meshes (H2): ep18 perception AUC 0.970 (scan template 0.957), ep24 0.795. Damaged-scan test (why mesh quality matters): clean 0.987, 3 mm noise 0.825, 5 mm inflation 0.608 (flat objects register flipped); scale errors cost nothing. Preliminary defect diagnostics (scratchpad/interact/defects, today, scans used for diagnosis only): thin regions are 7.8–15.5 mm thick in ours vs 1.6–7.1 mm in the scans; volume pitcher 1221 vs 288 cm3, lid 288 vs 82, dust pan 158 vs 65.

components.component: 2. Occluder-aware carving: hands, table and other tracked objects carve free space but never vote surface
components.what_we_do: Each depth sample whose 3-D point Pd falls in one of three occluder regions is flagged 'other': (a) within 3 cm of a MediaPipe hand bone or 4.5 cm of a 15 cm forearm segment (capsules in camera coordinates from hands.npz); (b) less than 1.5 cm above the support plane, re-fitted per frame (frame-0 RANSAC plane moved by VO, then re-fitted to samples within 3 cm and 1.2 cm, correction ≤ 10°); (c) within 12 mm of another tracked object's surface (KD-tree of 20k samples at its tracked pose). A flagged sample still updates voxels in front of it with +1 (free space) and never contributes its near-surface band (keep = ~other | sdf > trunc). In the library builds the other objects were the public scans posed by our tracks (scratchpad recon_library2.sh).
components.closest_prior_art: BundleSDF hybrid SDF (https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14158; verified, full text opened). It splits rays into 'uncertain free space' (background-mask or missing-depth pixels, including finger occlusions, pulled weakly to +epsilon), 'empty space' in front of the depth (L1 to +lambda) and a near-surface band. Co-Fusion/MaskFusion fuse only pixels with the object's label (verified, abstracts). Tzionas & Gall ICCV 2015 remove the hand by skin-colour segmentation before fusion (https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00529; verified, full text opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Occluders are identified geometrically in 3-D (hand skeleton capsules, a per-frame re-fitted plane, other objects' meshes at their tracked poses) instead of with 2-D masks. Their samples are fully trusted as free space, where BundleSDF gives such space only a weak epsilon pull. The idea of keeping occluded rays as free-space evidence without letting them vote surface is the same as BundleSDF's. Ours is a non-neural implementation, not a new principle.
components.evidence_it_matters: ep41 (pot): dropping table samples entirely gave AUC 0.711 (27.5° off); carve-only gave 0.988, then 0.998 with the ±30 cm cube. ep39 (dust pan): the per-frame table refit took the error from 131° (AUC 0.202) to 6.4° (0.823). Hand masking had no measurable effect on ep41 (0.9979 vs 0.9983) and is 7x slower. The other-object carve was not ablated separately; v1 on ep39 ('the extra sheet is the tabletop, not the hand').

components.component: 3. Below-table carving (the support half-space is free space)
components.what_we_do: In every frame, voxels more than 4 mm under that frame's re-fitted table plane get one free-space (+1) observation in the running average (--below_carve 0.004, default on). The frame-0 plane search was widened to a 65° cone around camera up because steep cameras in ep39/40 had a table normal 48–50° away. TSDF averaging lets the rare frame whose pose sinks the object be outvoted.
components.closest_prior_art: Tabletop shape completion that bounds unseen parts with the support plane, e.g. Bohg et al., 'Mind the Gap', ICRA 2011 (symmetry completion on a table, then simulation; metadata and search snippet only, not opened). ARM, Agnew et al. CoRL 2020: stability and connectivity priors for amodal reconstruction (https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.13146; verified, abstract). Kutulakos & Seitz space-carving theory: free-space constraints narrow the shape (search snippet only). NVIDIA mesh_to_usd fits a ground plane from the recording for the support pose (README opened, verified).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Applied as a soft, per-frame, voted constraint along a moving object's track rather than as a single cut. That is a sensible implementation detail, not a new idea.
components.evidence_it_matters: v1 filled the never-seen undersides down to 5.5 cm (pot) and 3.5 cm (dust pan) under the table, and mkref rejected the table on ep18. v2 lowest points are -0.2 to -0.6 cm (scans -0.1 to +0.2); pot 13.1x19.0x36.2 cm vs scan 13.2x18.9x35.7. Cost: dust pan registered AUC ep39 0.992 to 0.982, ep40 0.971 to 0.963, ep18 0.920 to 0.917.

components.component: 4. Automatic closing of never-observed space (fill vs near)
components.what_we_do: 'fill' marks every unknown region not connected to the grid border as inside. 'near' marks unknown voxels inside only within 3 voxels of observed-inside voxels, then fills enclosed cavities. 'auto' picks near when the never-observed share of the filled solid exceeds 0.5, else fill. The threshold was calibrated on 3 objects (pot 0.042, boards 0.14/0.015, dust pan 0.629).
components.closest_prior_art: Curless & Levoy 1996 hole filling: tessellate the boundary between observed-empty and never-observed ('unseen') regions (search snippet only; the Stanford page was unreachable from this VM). Visual hull / space carving (Kutulakos & Seitz; search snippet only).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Two closing rules with a data-driven switch on the unseen share. It is a pragmatic heuristic (one threshold, 3 calibration objects) that fixes a known failure of plain unseen-filling on thin plates (a wedge behind the plate). No prior art for this exact switch was searched hard, and it would not count as a contribution.
components.evidence_it_matters: Pot ep41: fill 0.998 vs near 0.986. Dust pan ep39: near 0.953 vs fill 0.82. Boards stay on fill with flip rate 0. The rule still closes container interiors and plate undersides: preliminary diagnostics show container and plate volumes 2.4–4.2x the scans.

components.component: 5. Meshing, clean-up and budget
components.what_we_do: Solid voxels become a ±1 field, which is Gaussian-blurred (sigma 0.8 voxel) and meshed by skimage marching cubes at 0. The continuous TSDF value is discarded at this step. The code keeps the component nearest the origin after a 2-voxel dilation, keeps pieces with ≥ 5 % of the main area within 15 cm, and decimates with the kit's budget_mesh to ≤ 4096 vertices and faces.
components.closest_prior_art: skimage marching cubes, scipy.ndimage, trimesh, and the kit's v2dlb.mesh_budget (off-the-shelf tools used as is).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing. One weakness found when reading the code: meshing the blurred binary occupancy instead of the TSDF zero crossing rounds edges and corners and sets a minimum wall of about 1 voxel plus the blur. That is consistent with the rounded sweeper underside and board edges that later needed flatten_base.
components.evidence_it_matters: Keeping only the largest piece cut the beige cup in half (registered AUC 0.84 to 0.42). The 5 %/15 cm rule gave 0.857 (scan 0.914). Rounded undersides and edges: sweeper footprint 0.3 cm2 with the centre of mass 3 cm outside it; board 1 footprint 0.1 cm2.

components.component: 6. Multi-episode fusion into one grid per object
components.what_we_do: Several episodes' poses, depth, hands and other objects are integrated into the same object-frame grid: pot 41/44/2/27, rack 12/13/27, blue cup 12/13/21/22, pitcher 21/22, dust pan 39/40/18, sweeper 18/31; boards, lid and beige cup from one episode each. Cross-episode registration is free because every episode's tracks share the object frame of the FoundationPose template, which was the public scan.
components.closest_prior_art: Multi-scan volumetric merging (Curless & Levoy 1996). NVIDIA's v2d_hoi_object_reconstruction 'two-stage scan (stationary → rotated → stationary)' merges stages by FoundationPose world-pose alignment so the bottom becomes visible (README opened, verified).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing methodological. The alignment problem that NVIDIA's module solves explicitly is bypassed here by scan-template tracks. That is a provenance dependency (A-lite), not an innovation.
components.evidence_it_matters: Pot fused over 41/44/2/27, scored on held-out pot episodes: ep42 0.958, ep43 0.979, ep45 0.964 (scan 0.986/0.993/0.966). A one-episode run reproduced the v5 mesh exactly (consistency check). No single- vs multi-episode ablation was found in the docs.

components.component: 7. Vertex colours from video (mesh_color.py)
components.what_we_do: Each vertex is projected into every 4th rectified-left mono frame. It is counted visible where the stereo depth agrees within 1 cm, and its grey value is the median of those samples. Unseen vertices get the global median. The purpose is FoundationPose's appearance terms.
components.closest_prior_art: Standard per-vertex colour mapping with a visibility test and robust (median) blending. Waechter et al. 2014, 'Let there be color!', is the usual view-selection reference (from memory, not verified here). BundleSDF also bakes texture (verified, paper).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing.
components.evidence_it_matters: None measured. There is no ablation of colour vs no colour for tracking. ep41 pot: 90 % of vertices seen, 50 s.

components.component: 8. Flattened undersides and standing edges (flatten_base.py; library_v3 sweeper, library_v4 boards)
components.what_we_do: For one object at one perceived resting frame of our own reference, take the world up in the mesh frame. Move vertices within 8 mm of the lowest point along it onto one plane 4 mm above that point (cut 4 mm, fill 4 mm). Chosen by hand per object and episode (sweeper ep18 f0; board 1 ep24 f150; board 2 ep24 f250), validated by an assist-off CPU drop test.
components.closest_prior_art: Make It Stand (Prévost et al., SIGGRAPH 2013): deform volume or shape so a model balances on chosen bases (metadata verified via Semantic Scholar, content from search snippets). Atlas3D (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.18515), DSO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.22677) and PhyRecon (https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16666): stability-aware geometry via simulation (verified, abstracts). PhysComp, Guo et al. NeurIPS 2024 (search snippet only). Closest in this ecosystem: NVIDIA mesh_to_usd. Its 'principal-6-support' levels the largest downward coplanar patch, its 'recorded-support' mode takes the up vector from a stable window of tracked poses plus the fitted ground plane, and it runs a drop test with a standing check. It validates the mesh but does not edit it (README opened, verified). The plane cut is also the routine 'flat base' operation in 3D-printing preparation.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Our up vector comes from our own perceived rest pose, and the geometry is edited for an RL policy's simulator rather than for printing. As implemented it is a manual per-object, per-episode patch (the docs say so) and is cruder than Make It Stand, Atlas3D or DSO. It is not a contribution.
components.evidence_it_matters: ep18, combined with stable-pose rest settling and the start fix (one seed, 6 evaluations): 0.345 ± 0.046 (base) to 0.715 ± 0.240, with 5 of 6 rollouts at 0.79–0.84 and SP/MP 1. The same setup with the rounded sweeper scored 0.368 ± 0.069, so the gain comes from the mesh. CPU: sweeper tilt 17.6° by step 4 became ≤ 0.7° for 9 steps. ep24 board edges (library_v4) are untested on GPU; board 1 is only marginally stable (+0.1 mm).

components.component: 9. Simulator asset preparation (make_assets.py)
components.what_we_do: Colourless geometry-only copy (visual = collision), URDF in the public-asset layout, placeholder mass 0.3 kg, centre of mass and inertia of a uniform thin shell from 20k surface samples. No separate collision mesh; FlashCHORD/Newton runs CoACD itself.
components.closest_prior_art: The public Track 3 assets (same 0.3 kg convention). NVIDIA mesh_to_usd defaults to 0.3 kg with collider-derived inertia (README opened, verified). Competitor tianny0078 builds hollow cup colliders from 64 convex wall wedges plus a bottom (README opened, verified). Scalable Real2Sim (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00370; verified, abstract) identifies collision geometry and inertia.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: The colourless copy works around a loader behaviour we found ourselves (Newton splits a coloured mesh into one shape per face colour). It is a useful engineering finding, not research. The shell inertia matches the organisers' convention but is less physical than solid-volume inertia for handled tools.
components.evidence_it_matters: With coloured meshes a board became 174 open fragments; CoACD ran > 10 min and the 4096-world ep24 build was SIGKILLed twice. Colourless: 1 watertight shape; 64 worlds build in 4.2 s with 0.61 GB.

components.component: 10. Interaction-aware reconstruction (stage 8, in progress; owner's idea): non-penetration at co-located frames, empty swept volumes, support patches, fingertip contacts as surface constraints
components.what_we_do: Not yet in the pipeline. What exists is a census (scratchpad/interact/census.py, today). For every frame and ordered object pair it measures the overlap volume, penetration depth (EDT) and surface distance between our meshes posed by our tracks, plus per-voxel 'entered-by-the-other-object' counts, with the scans posed by the same tracks as a diagnostic floor. Defect diagnostics (thickness, volume, IoU vs scan) are also run. The design (three variants, judge, critic) is still pending.
components.closest_prior_art: Scene and pose level: Picasso (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08058; non-penetration and contact-graph rejection sampling over pose and shape), φ-Scene (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21596; SDF penetration resolution then rigid settling), Real-to-Sim for cluttered scenes (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12633; contact graph plus differentiable simulation, poses and physical properties), PhyRecon (https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16666), ARM (https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.13146). Hand contact: In-Hand 3D Object Reconstruction from monocular RGB (https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.16425; penetration and attraction constraints in contact regions), HOLD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18448), MagicHOI (https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05506), Tzionas & Gall 2015 (contacts used as registration correspondences, not surface samples; full text verified). Touch as surface samples: NeuralFeels (https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13469), Smith et al. 2020 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.03778). Swept free space: robot end-effector sweeps certify free space (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21410). Mating: Neural Shape Mating (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14886). All verified by arXiv abstract unless noted.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Prior physical-plausibility work fixes a single static view (Picasso, φ-Scene, 2602.12633), adjusts mainly poses, or uses hand contact with one held object. The plan here is different. It uses a whole manipulation video's sequence of rigid co-located configurations (assembly, nesting, lid on pot, tool on dust pan), each object's volume swept through the other's frame, resting support, and human fingertips as virtual touch. Together these constrain the shapes of two objects over time, with simulator validity for an RL tracking policy as the target. No paper combining these was found. Searches covered: hand contact as a surface constraint for occluded completion; multi-object non-penetration from video; swept-volume free-space carving; support-plane or resting-pose shape inference. Each ingredient has prior art, so this is a new combination and only a hypothesis until it is built and scored.
components.evidence_it_matters: Preliminary census (today, scratchpad). ep24 boards: max overlap 9.0 cm3 with our v2/v4 meshes vs 4.0 cm3 with the scans at the same tracks (the tracking-error floor); ep23 9.0 vs 3.1. The work log measured 13.5 cm3 at the assembled pose, and the boards' slots are missing. Container pairs (ep0 pot+lid 122 cm3, ep11 nested cups 71 cm3) cannot yet be judged, because the non-watertight scans were solidified by hole filling. No score yet. ep24 stays at about 0.31 with every variant tried, and the docs attribute its ceiling to the stand-up and assembly.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Thin-shell-capable fusion. Use a sparse high-resolution TSDF (VDBFusion or nvblox; 1–1.5 mm voxels near the surface, 3–4 mm truncation, weights decreasing with depth squared and grazing angle) and mesh the TSDF zero crossing directly instead of the blurred binary occupancy. Where a surface is seen from both sides (rims, cup interiors, the lid), keep an open shell and give it a thickness measured at the rims ('solidify').
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: VDBFusion (Vizzo et al., Sensors 2022; search snippet only); nvblox (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.00626; verified, abstract); Curless & Levoy weighting; TRELLIS.2's O-Voxel represents open and thin surfaces (https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14692; verified, abstract); the competitor tianny0078 uses procedurally hollowed cups (README verified).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The largest measured defect is thickness. Diagnostics: 8–15.5 mm walls vs 1.6–3.5 mm in the scans; lid and pitcher volumes 3.5–4.2x. In the damaged-scan test, 5 mm inflation alone dropped mean registered AUC from 0.987 to 0.608 and flipped flat objects. Filled cavities also make cups and pot+lid overlap in sim (ep11 71 cm3, ep0 122 cm3).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: CPU or a cheap GPU, about 1–2 days of work, no rental needed. Risk: FoundationStereo noise at 0.4–0.8 m may not support mm walls (holes, double surfaces); budget_mesh decimation to 4096 faces may erase the gain; open shells need watertight solidification before CoACD.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Rebuild lid, dust pan, pitcher, both cups and the pot. Reject if, against the scans (diagnostic only), the median thickness in scan-thin regions stays above 6 mm, or if the registered AUC or the 8-seed flip rate on ep2/11/21/39/41 does not improve over library_v2 by more than noise (about 0.01).

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Generative completion that must obey our observations. Generate candidates with Hunyuan3D-Omni (point-cloud or voxel conditioning from our TSDF), SAM 3D Objects, TRELLIS.2 or Amodal3R from the clearest frames. Scale and pose them by ICP to our observed surface. Reject or deform any candidate that puts material in voxels we observed as free, then merge: observed surface wins where seen, the generated shape where never seen.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Hunyuan3D-Omni (https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21245), SAM 3D (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16624), TRELLIS.2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14692), Amodal3R (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13439), DiffComplete partial-scan completion (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16329), all verified by abstract. The organisers' HOI module has a SAM3D mode with silhouette scale estimation (README verified). Do as I Do uses SAM3D meshes (local README).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: It fills undersides, cavities, flat bases, sharp edges and possibly the board slots with plausible geometry instead of fill/near heuristics and hand patches. The leaders' CD-O (0.065 and 0.313 cm) is far below our 0.22–1.15 cm.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About $3–6 of GPU for 11 objects plus 2–3 days of integration. Risks: hallucinated detail; scale and axis errors; licences (Hunyuan territorial, SAM licence, nvdiffrast non-commercial in TRELLIS) against the Apache-2.0 release rule; and the free-space check depends on our track quality.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Per object on public episodes, compare the registered AUC (8 seeds), the flip rate and the diagnostic CD against library_v2. Reject the route if it is worse for half or more of the objects, or if any chosen candidate violates more than 1 % of the observed free-space voxels.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Parametric and CAD shape priors fitted to our observations: surfaces of revolution (axis + profile + wall thickness) for the cups, pot, lid and pitcher body; extrusion/CSG (box minus slots) for the boards; swept tubes for handles. Object names are allowed at inference, so the template family can be chosen by name.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Bohg et al. 2011 symmetry completion (snippet only); Thrun & Wegbreit 2005 'Shape from symmetry' and Kroemer et al. 2012 extrusion completion (snippets only); CAD-Recode point cloud to CadQuery code (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14042) and Point2CAD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04962), both verified by abstract.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: It gives flat bases and sharp edges automatically, which yields stable rest and standing poses (the ep18 lesson: 0.345 to 0.715 once the sweeper could stand) without per-episode flattening. It also gives true thin walls, open cavities and the boards' interlocking slots, the documented ep24 blockers.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: CPU only, about 2–4 days. Risk: shapes off-template (pitcher spout, rack lattice, sweeper bristles). Mitigate by blending, with the template only where the TSDF is unknown. Judges may view per-category templates as less general (Innovation award angle).
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Reject if the registered AUC or flip rate is worse than library_v2 on the template objects (public episodes 2/11/21/23/24/41), or if the assist-off drop test still finds no stable pose within 5° of a perceived resting pose.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Silhouette carving: soft visual-hull votes from the SAM2 masks we already compute, on both mono cameras and cam_a, fused into the same grid. Pixels outside the mask carve space in front of the observed depth. Mask pixels near hands get low confidence, as in BundleSDF's uncertain free space.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Hernández Esteban & Schmitt 2004, 'Silhouette and stereo fusion for 3D object modeling' (search snippet only); Kutulakos & Seitz space carving (snippet only); BundleSDF's uncertain-free-space treatment of mask background (verified, full text).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: recon_mesh uses no masks at all. Silhouettes are sharp where stereo depth blurs: thin plates, edges and handles. The edge filter we tried instead removed plate edges (dust pan 0.953 to 0.880).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Low: masks exist and this is CPU work, about 1 day. Risk: mask errors around fingers carve real material (thin handles disappear), and three-camera synchronisation and rolling shutter on cam_a.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On ep39 (dust pan), ep2 (lid) and ep23 (boards), reject if the diagnostic thickness and registered AUC do not improve, or if any object loses a part, as measured by the scan-to-ours p90 distance growing.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Physics-in-the-loop shape identification ('analysis by simulation'). Parametrise only the never-observed parts (underside offset and tilt, edge bevel, slot depth and width, wall thickness). Choose the values with which CPU MuJoCo replays of our own rest segments, stacks and assemblies reproduce our tracked poses (no drift, tip-over or penetration), with no ground truth. This generalises flatten_base from one manual cut into an automatic search.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Galileo (Wu et al., NeurIPS 2015: MCMC through a physics engine to infer hidden properties; snippet only); PhyRecon (verified); DSO's simulator feedback (verified); Real-to-Sim for cluttered scenes with a differentiable rigid-body sim (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12633; verified); NVIDIA mesh_to_usd's recorded-support drop test (verified).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: It turns the hand-made per-object patches (sweeper, boards), which the owner flagged as non-robust, into one rule for all 20 eval episodes. Because it uses the simulator the policy trains in, it optimises exactly the failure mode that cost ep18 about 0.37 AUC.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: CPU, about 3–5 days. Risks: non-identifiability, since many shapes are stable; overfitting to tracking noise, since objects float 1–4 cm in our references; and it can mask perception errors.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On the 12 two-object public episodes, reject if the assist-off drop-test failures and census overlaps do not fall by at least half while the registered AUC is unchanged (±0.01), or if a GPU A/B on ep18 and ep24 shows no gain over library_v3/v4.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Support tangency from all rest segments, across episodes and including eval videos at inference. Every frame where an object rests on the table gives a supporting plane in the object frame: the object lies entirely above it and touches it with a patch containing the centre-of-mass projection. Intersect the half-spaces (bound) and add the touch constraint (fill to the plane) automatically, instead of using one manual frame.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: FlipToSee stable-placement prior (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20078; verified, abstract); SO-SLAM support-plane constraints (snippet only); our own below_carve (half-space only) and flatten_base (one frame).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: It recovers undersides and edges the cameras never see from information we already have. Each new resting orientation (lying, standing, flipped) adds a face, so more episodes give a better shape, which a TSDF cannot achieve for unseen faces.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Low CPU cost, about 1–2 days. Main risk: our references float 1–4 cm above the table (measured), so the touch constraint would grow the mesh down into air. It needs rest-pose refinement (or using depth of the table contact line) first.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Reject if, after construction, the objects do not stand within 2° and 3 mm for 20 assist-off steps at every perceived rest segment of public episodes 12, 18, 23, 24 and 27, or if the registered AUC drops more than 0.01.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Fingertips as virtual touch, with uncertainty. In stable grasp segments, contact pads of our refined 3-D hands become noisy surface samples, and the hand volume becomes free space, inside a probabilistic implicit surface (GPIS-like). This puts surface on faces the cameras never see, such as board undersides held from below or handle backs.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: NeuralFeels visuo-tactile neural field (https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13469), Smith et al. vision+touch (https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.03778), In-Hand 3D Object Reconstruction penetration and attraction constraints (https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.16425), all verified by abstract; GPIS visuo-haptic fusion (Björkman/Dragiev; snippet only).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: It is the only cue for surfaces under the hand (the 'contact region' that monocular HOI work reports as its main error) and for slots touched during assembly.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: CPU, about 2 days. Risk: our hand depth is coarse. ep24 hands were squashed into the board (wrist-to-tip 3.8–5.2 cm), and robot-reference fingertips sat 16–20 mm p95 inside objects, which is noise larger than the features we want.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: First measure the fingertip-to-surface error on surfaces we did observe. Reject outright if the median exceeds 5 mm. Otherwise reject if the diagnostic distance on never-observed regions (board undersides, ep24) does not improve.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Mating and assembly carving for long co-located pairs. Where two tracked objects stay rigidly together for many frames (ep23/24 boards, lid on pot, nested cups, sweeper on dust pan), compute the overlap at the robust mean relative pose. Assign each overlapping voxel to the object with the weaker occupancy evidence (fewer inside observations, more free observations), which carves slots and cavities.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Neural Shape Mating (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14886); Picasso non-penetration with a contact graph (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08058); φ-Scene SDF penetration resolution (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21596). All verified by abstract. Analogy: archaeological fragment reassembly, where the fit itself reveals hidden geometry.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: It targets the documented ep24 blocker (13.5 cm3 overlap at the assembled pose, no slots) and the eval twin ep25 automatically, plus container nesting, without per-object patches.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: CPU, about 1–2 days on top of the census. Risk: tracking error (the scans posed by our tracks still overlap 3–4 cm3) would carve real material. Only overlap above that floor should be carved.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Reject if the overlap at assembled frames does not fall to the scan floor (about 3–4 cm3), if the diagnostic CD worsens, or if a GPU A/B on ep24 shows no change in the stand-up/assembly segment (board 1 about f102, board 2 about f117).

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Solve joint tracking and reconstruction ourselves, without the public scans as tracking templates. Use object-centric 2DGS with gsplat (Apache-2.0), or BundleSDF / 6DOPE-GS style pose-graph plus neural field, starting from a frame-0 mask, then re-track with the result.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: BundleSDF (verified, full text); 6DOPE-GS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.01543); 2DGS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17888); Scalable Real2Sim's alpha-transparent object-centric meshes (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00370); EgoAERO asset-free tracking and reconstruction from egocentric RGB-D (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08057). All verified by abstract.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: It removes the A-lite provenance dependency (the FAQ asks participants to reconstruct objects to generate trajectories) and strengthens the Innovation-award story. Joint pose refinement also removes the time-varying pose error that blurs our TSDF.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: GPU: about $5–15 for the 11 objects plus several days of work. Licence risk (BundleSDF is non-commercial; gsplat is fine). Accuracy risk: BundleSDF reports CD 0.57 cm on HO3D and 1.16 cm on YCBInEOAT, no better than our current meshes.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On public episodes 2, 11, 18, 21, 23, 24, 39 and 41, keep the scan-template-built library if the scan-free meshes lose more than 0.02 mean registered AUC or add any 8-seed flips.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Fuse the eval videos into each object's mesh at inference: library meshes plus observations from the 20 eval clips, tracked with our own meshes. The same objects appear in new orientations there (lids flipped, boards stood up, spoon in 10 episodes).
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Multi-session mapping and lifelong SLAM. NVIDIA's two-stage scan, which rotates the object to reveal the bottom (README verified).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Each new resting orientation exposes faces never seen in public episodes, and eval-specific geometry is what the hidden-scan registration scores. It is inference-legal: video only, no ground truth, no tuning on eval results.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Low marginal cost: eval perception is already planned on one box, about $2–3 at about 4 min per episode. Risk: a bad eval track corrupts the shared mesh. Gate each episode's contribution by agreement with the existing mesh (observed-surface residual) and keep per-episode versions.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Simulate it on public data by holding out episodes (for example, build the pot from 41/44 and add 2/27 as 'eval'). Reject if adding the held-out episodes does not raise the registered AUC on the remaining held-out episodes (42/43/45), or if it raises the flip rate.

stage: Stage 4: human-to-robot hand retargeting and reference cleaning (pipeline/mkref.py + organiser's E2S, pipeline/contact_retarget.py incl. rest_settle/stable_ups, pipeline/robot_clearance.py). Verdict: nothing in this stage is novel. The kinematic core is off-the-shelf (NVIDIA E2S). Every cleaning step is standard practice or an adaptation of a published method. The closest prior art is EgoCPT (arXiv 2610.17572, 13 Oct 2026). It works in our setting: egocentric video, FoundationPose objects, Sharpa hands and noisy hand poses. It refines both hands' 56 DoF under joint-limit and penetration constraints, which is the same step as our contact_retarget.py. EgoCPT also adds contact sampling and force allocation, which we lack. The thing most specific to us is how we check penetration: the solver asks the same MuJoCo collision engine and convex pieces that the FlashCHORD evaluator uses, so a frame that is clean in the solver is also clean when the evaluator resets to it. That is a careful adaptation of a known trick: mink, SPIDER and DexMachina all use the simulator's own collision handling. Measured effect: the references became physically clean and the rollouts became consistent, but the 4-episode mean barely moved (0.577 to 0.587). This matches the literature's finding that cleaning a reference without physics is necessary but not enough (EgoCPT, OmniHOI, SPIDER). Method note: WebFetch could not resolve hosts here (DNS error). Primary sources were opened with curl through the proxy instead: arXiv abstract pages, plus arXiv HTML for DexMachina, EgoCPT and OmniHOI. Code was read in the scratchpad clones (repos/: spider, mink, DexForge, do-as-i-do, pyroki). Items marked 'search only' were confirmed to exist by web search, but their pages were not opened.

components.component: Kinematic retargeting: organiser's E2S (ego_recon_to_sharpa.py)
components.what_we_do: NVIDIA's E2S runs unchanged in a subprocess (mkref stage d), with shims we added: hppfcl aliased to coal, a kinematics-only BuildFromMJCF, and a schema patch. It is pink/pinocchio IK (daqp solver, 100 iterations per frame) on the Sharpa MJCF as a free-flyer. Frame tasks (position cost, orientation cost): wrist hand_C_MC (0.2, 0.2); thumb, index, middle and ring tips (1.0, 0.05-0.1); pinky tip (0.5, 0.1); MP sites from the MCP joints (0.1, 0). Human keypoints are scaled 1.2x about the wrist. Our input is MediaPipe joints lifted with stereo depth instead of MANO, plus anatomical frames we compute (hand_rotations) and 10 warm-up copies of frame 0. Optional: wrist cost 3.0 (variant 'c').
components.closest_prior_art: DexPilot https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.03135 (verified, abstract). AnyTeleop / dex-retargeting https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04577 (verified, abstract). DexMV https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877 (verified, abstract). GeoRT https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07541 (verified, abstract; neural keypoint retargeter with pinch and self-collision terms, 1 kHz). OmniRetarget https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.26633 (verified, abstract) describes our exact failure: retargeting artifacts such as penetration when keypoints are scaled.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing in the method. The only differences are plumbing: we feed it MANO-free MediaPipe joints, and we tried a wrist-cost setting. It knows neither the robot's collision geometry nor the objects.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured: the E2S robot hand sits 16-20 mm (p95) inside objects at 63-88 % of frames (ep12/27/18/24). Resetting to a reference frame pops an object in one physics step at 63-89 % of start frames. Wrist cost 3.0 had a failed single-seed run on ep12 (0.604) and is not adopted without more seeds.

components.component: Human-hand pre-cleaning before IK (mkref stages a-b: table frame and object snap, park or fill missing hands, lead-in, hand separation, joint-centre depenetration)
components.what_we_do: Table frame: RANSAC plane on frame-0 stereo depth, with resting objects snapped to it. A side with less than 10 % valid frames is parked 30 cm back and 25 cm up. Invalid runs are filled by holding the last pose, or by 'attach': the hand rides rigidly with the object it touches at the run boundary, blended between the two boundaries. Lead-in: a hand first seen at t1 > 0 now starts 15 cm out and 10 cm up and moves in over the 10 frames before t1. Hand separation: rigid per-frame shifts keep every left-right joint pair at least 4 cm apart; the unmeasured hand moves, away from the other hand and upward; up to 5 rounds with 5-frame box smoothing. Depenetration: joint centres are kept at least 6 mm outside the object meshes (cited from ContactOpt) and above the measured table disc; a joint pinned between table and object goes to the object's top.
components.closest_prior_art: Mocap gap filling: Vicon Nexus rigid-body and pattern fill (search only, Vicon docs). Physics-free hand-object depenetration: ContactOpt https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07267 (verified, abstract). Hand settle before the episode: Do as I Do https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19333 (verified, abstract; code read: warmup_steps 600 in retargeting configs). Constraint correction blended into neighbouring frames: Kovar, Schreiner and Gleicher, Footskate Cleanup, SCA 2002, https://research.cs.wisc.edu/graphics/Gallery/kovar.vol/Cleanup (search only).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Engineering fixes for our failure cases: the hand unseen at the start of ep24, two robot hands overlapping, MediaPipe dropouts. No new method.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured: lead-in plus 4 cm separation took ep24 from 0.080 to 0.232 (single rollouts; registered AUC). Depenetration keeps human fingertips outside objects (0 % inside), but the clearance does not survive IK onto the larger Sharpa hand. Raising it from 6 to 10 mm pushed one fingertip from 3.5 to 8 mm into the board.

components.component: FlashCHORD contact labels (mkref stage e)
components.what_we_do: 16 probes per hand: 5 tip sites, 5 DP sites, thumb MCP_VL, 4 MP sites and the palm mean, all taken from the E2S robot frames. Each probe gets its closest point on our object mesh. A slot is active if it is within 18 mm (palm 28 mm), the object is within ±20 frames of moving, and the contact lasts at least 2 frames. Stored: world-frame position, inward normal, part id. Code read: contact_retarget.py rewrites only the wrist, finger, frame and (with rest_settle) object columns. The labels are therefore NOT recomputed after contact retargeting or rest settling. They can be off by the wrist shift (up to 6 cm) and the object settle shift (2-4 cm).
components.closest_prior_art: FlashCHORD's own contact_labels.py convention, which uses the same thresholds (repo note docs/research/notes/22). CHORD https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00033 (verified, abstract). DexMachina contact rewards https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24853 (verified, HTML: N_c = 50 contacts assigned to the nearest links). C2Dex and DexForge recompute robot-side contacts from stable anchors (C2Dex https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07045 verified, abstract; DexForge code read).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: A re-implementation of the organiser's convention. It drops the stale-label gap that prior pipelines close by recomputing contacts from the final robot reference.
components.evidence_it_matters: No direct measurement. Literature: CHORD's contact-wrench reward collapses at about 25 mm / 25 deg of contact noise, which is the size of our stale-label offsets (per the earlier repo review, docs/research/contact-retargeting-2026-10-21.md).

components.component: Contact-anchored retargeting on robot geometry (contact_retarget.py main solve)
components.what_we_do: Per hand and per frame, starting from the E2S solution. (1) Targets: each human MediaPipe fingertip within 25 mm of an object surface is projected onto it, using the trilinear SDF over that body's convex collision pieces at 2.5 mm voxels, and placed 1 mm outside. Runs shorter than 3 frames are dropped. Each run is smoothed with a 5-frame box filter in the object frame. (2) Unknowns: a 6-D wrist correction, bounded to ±6 cm and ±0.5 rad per axis from E2S, plus 22 finger joint offsets within the joint limits. These are solved by a small Levenberg-Marquardt loop with central finite differences (8 iterations) on Newton CPU forward kinematics. Residuals: each target matched to its nearest collision-surface sample on that finger's distal link (any side of the link, not a pad region), with a pseudo-Huber pull beyond 15 mm; penetration (next component); distance from E2S (scales 2 cm / 0.3 rad / 0.5 rad); continuity with the previous frame. (3) Frames without contacts or penetration decay back toward E2S (factor 0.8). Frames are solved forward in time, left hand then right; the right hand sees the solved left. All 67 robot frames are rewritten by rigid offsets to their links. CPU time: 3-6 min per episode.
components.closest_prior_art: EgoCPT https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17572 (verified, abstract and HTML). Same setting: egocentric video, FoundationPose, Sharpa, noisy hand poses. Its pose refinement over 56 DoF minimises fingertip-to-contact distance under joint limits and penetration d >= -eps, then smooths. Unlike ours, it samples contact candidates near the robot fingertips (rejection sampling) and keeps only those that pass force allocation. Contact-Anchored Retargeting + residual RL https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24093 (verified, abstract). C2Dex (stable object-frame contacts, Laplacian transfer; verified, abstract). DexForge https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06331 (verified, abstract; code read, contactaware.yaml: contact on at 10 mm, minimum duration 8 frames, 80 % stable fraction, pad region axial <= 0.5 and palmar cosine >= 0.75, palm weights scaled down during contact, SQP with trust regions). PyRoki examples/09_hand_retargeting.py (code read: contact-point costs over the whole DexYCB trajectory). TopoRetarget https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16272 and DexOAK https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26762 (both verified, abstract).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Mostly the fit to our evaluator: (a) penetration is measured on the evaluator's own scene (next component); (b) the wrist correction is hard-bounded around E2S, on the principle that a contact the hand cannot reach without a large move is more likely a wrong target than a wrong hand. Weaker than prior art in documented ways.
