Targets are snapped per frame from 1-2 cm-noisy fingertips instead of consolidated object-frame anchors (C2Dex: removing cross-frame consolidation drops end-to-end success from 57.8 % to 17.8 %). The gate is permissive (25 mm, 3 frames; DexForge uses 10 mm, 8 frames). There is no pad-region, normal or sidedness term. There is no wrench or force-allocation check (EgoCPT: contact and pose refinement without force allocation 1/10 vs 10/10 with it). There is no grip preload, the hands are solved one after the other rather than jointly, and the contact labels are not recomputed.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured (simulator check, CPU). ep24: frames with a hand more than 2 mm inside something 242 -> 62 of 275; penetration p95 20.1 -> 6.0 mm; median one-step pop 8.6 -> 2.9 deg. ep18: about 77 % -> 41 of 361 frames; p95 16 -> 2.7 mm. Registered ADD-AUC, 6 evaluations each: ep12 0.725 -> 0.790; ep27 0.942 -> 0.911; ep18 0.345 -> 0.319 (s42) / 0.361 (s43); ep24 0.297 -> 0.307 / 0.306. The spread shrinks (ep12 ±0.067 -> ±0.023; ep24 ±0.055 -> ±0.002-0.018). 4-episode mean 0.577 -> 0.587. Cleaner and more consistent references, but not a general score gain.

components.component: Penetration oracle: the evaluator's own collision engine inside the solve (MjPen)
components.what_we_do: MjPen takes the mj_model that Newton hands to MuJoCo Warp: the same convex pieces of our meshes, the table and both hands. It sets all geom margins to 1 mm, puts the scene at reference frame f (objects included, rest-settled if enabled), and runs CPU mujoco mj_kinematics + mj_collision (0.3-0.7 ms per call). Per collision geom of the hand being solved, it returns max(0, 1 mm - depth) over that geom's contacts with objects, the table and the other hand. This goes into the least-squares residual (scaled by 2 mm). For hands with primitive collision shapes, surface samples come from MuJoCo geom types.
components.closest_prior_art: mink CollisionAvoidanceLimit (code read, src/mink/limits/collision_avoidance_limit.py): IK constraint on mj_geomDistance between geom pairs, defaults 5 mm minimum and 5 cm detection; used by Do as I Do's replay (code read). SPIDER https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.09484 (verified, abstract; code read, spider/preprocess/ik.py): IK runs as a MuJoCo simulation with mocap-weld equality constraints, contacts optionally enabled. DexMachina (verified, HTML): 'replay the retargeted joint values as soft control targets in simulation while keeping the object fixed ... record the achieved joint values'.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: The oracle is the exact collision pipeline and decomposition of the FlashCHORD/Newton scene that the official evaluator resets into, not a separately built MJCF. A frame that is clean in the solve is therefore clean at evaluator reset, with no geometry mismatch. That is careful engineering on a known idea, not a new method. Cost: max(0, .) kinks force finite differences, hence a hand-written LM instead of analytic Jacobians.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured: the first version used hull samples against an SDF capped at 64 cells per axis (about 1 cm voxels on boards) and left fingers inside thin boards. With MjPen, ep24 p95 penetration fell to 6.0 mm and ep18 to 2.7 mm (see the previous component). An unbounded wrist drifted 17 cm on ep24's right hand, which is why the ±6 cm bound exists.

components.component: Robot clearance by one-step simulator contacts with anchored temporal smoothing (robot_clearance.py)
components.what_we_do: For every frame: reset the FlashCHORD environment (1 world) to frame t, take one physics step and read the MuJoCo contacts. Compute the smallest wrist translation that clears each hand's contacts with objects, table and the other hand by 1 mm (projection over contact normals; hand-hand contacts split half and half). Then smooth per hand: argmin sum |d_t - need_t|^2 + lam |d_{t+1} - d_t|^2, a tridiagonal solve in which clean frames anchor to 0. Repeat for up to 3 rounds. Translation only. It was superseded by contact_retarget and is now used as a diagnostic; its settle() is reused by rest_settle.
components.closest_prior_art: DexMachina's retargeting post-processing, where the simulator resolves collisions (verified, HTML). Footskate cleanup, which blends per-frame constraint corrections into the unconstrained neighbouring frames (Kovar et al., SCA 2002; search only). Physics 'dynamics filter' for mocap (Yamane and Nakamura, ICRA 2000; search only).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: The fix uses contacts from the evaluator's own reset and step, with anchored least-squares blending. Each part is classic.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured on ep24: dirty frames 242 -> 87; p95 penetration 20.1 -> 13.3 mm; dirty start frames 49 -> 31 of 55; frame-0 pop 6.2 -> 0.8 deg. Fingers wrapped through objects remained, which led to contact_retarget.

components.component: Rest settling: resting objects seated on the table and turned to the nearest quasi-static stable pose (contact_retarget --rest_settle: rest_settle + stable_ups)
components.what_we_do: Per object and frame, the object counts as 'free' when all of these hold: its lowest collision point is within 5 cm of the table top; it does not rest on another object (its lowest points are more than 1 cm from the other objects' SDFs); and either no human fingertip is within 3 cm or it is static over ±2 frames (< 4 mm/frame and < 2 deg/frame). Stable poses: faces of the convex hull of the collision pieces whose footprint contains the projection of the centre of mass (volume-weighted centroid of the pieces) with a 2 mm margin. Free frames get the minimal rotation (heading kept) onto the nearest stable 'up' if within 15 deg, then the vertical shift onto the table. Both are smoothed by the anchored least squares above (lam 4; other frames pull to 0). This rewrites the object reference trajectories that the policy tracks, and the robot hand is then re-solved against the settled scene. Uses only our own perception and hands.
components.closest_prior_art: DexForge (code read, contactaware/solver/ground.py and resting.py): object ground-clearance QP with temporal smoothing (object_ground_qp_smooth 200); resting detection by velocity thresholds; first-frame settle in MuJoCo Warp, then a rigid correction of the trajectory with the hand carried along. PhysPose https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23587 (verified, abstract): post-processing that enforces non-penetration and gravity (no levitation) on 6D pose estimates. trimesh.poses.compute_stable_poses (source read: quasi-static stable resting poses on a plane, with probabilities). Footskate-style blending (search only).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Applied to every rest segment of the episode, gated by hand proximity and speed, with an object-on-object exclusion. The stable-pose turn is a quasi-static test (the same theory as trimesh), not a physics settle. It edits the tracked object reference rather than only the pose estimate. No component is new, and DexForge already combines ground QP, resting detection and smoothing.
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured, mixed. ep12 kr (rest settle + stable pose) 0.740 ± 0.032 vs 0.790 ± 0.023 without it (one seed, -0.05). ep24 kri 0.312 vs ki 0.318. ep18 height-only kri 0.368. ep18 with a flattened sweeper mesh plus the stable-pose turn (kfi): 0.715 ± 0.240 (5 of 6 rollouts 0.79-0.84) vs 0.345 base, confounded with the stage-3 mesh fix. CPU drop test: ep12 cup seated 0.4 cm / 3.5 deg; ep27 rack drop 1.05 -> 0.03 cm. It pays off only where an object cannot stand by itself.

components.component: Reference-variant portfolio chosen by a ground-truth-free sim score (E2S vs contact-retargeted vs rest-settled; stage-4 outputs fed to stage-6 selection)
components.what_we_do: Build several candidate references per episode, train each, and keep the one whose rollouts best match our own reference (sim_vs_ref, no mocap). Applied per episode by auto_ep.sh.
components.closest_prior_art: Selecting physics-refined trajectories by simulated rollout cost is the core loop of SPIDER (verified, abstract and code) and OmniHOI https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10855 (verified, HTML: CMA-ES over keyframe offsets, scored by rollouts). Generic model selection on a proxy validation metric.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: It selects among whole trained policies rather than among trajectory samples, which is expensive (one training per variant).
components.evidence_it_matters: Measured: sim_vs_ref ranked base vs retargeting the same way as the true score on all 4 episodes (one tie). Earlier, sim_vs_ref correlated 0.98 with the mocap score over 8 evaluations of one policy.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Refine the hard windows with physics in the loop. Run OmniHOI-style CMA-ES or SPIDER-style annealed sampling over wrist and finger keyframe offsets in FlashCHORD's own Newton scene, object assist OFF. Cost function: object tracking of our perceived trajectory + contact gap + penetration + E2S prior. Start with ep24's stand-up (about f95-f135) and ep18's sweep strokes. Train RL on the physically executed reference, or use its states as resets.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: SPIDER https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.09484 (verified; per the repo review, kinematic ADD-AUC 11 -> 57 with physics refinement). OmniHOI https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10855 (verified HTML: CMA-ES per keyframe in rolling horizons; table shows SharpaWave results). Do as I Do warmup (code read).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Our references are kinematically clean but dynamically unvalidated. Every ep24 variant (0.306-0.318) fails exactly where a board is lifted and stood on its edge, and cleaning the reference without physics did not move the mean in any of the papers above either.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-4 days of code. GPU about $2-5 per episode (estimate). Risks: Newton rollout throughput for about 1k samples x 30 iterations; the task may be infeasible for the Sharpa with our board meshes (slots still missing); sample-based search can exploit simulator artefacts.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On the ep24 stand-up window, the best refined open-loop rollout must keep board 2 within 2 cm / 15 deg of our reference for 30 or more frames. If no sample achieves this, the idea is falsified for this geometry. If it passes, RL on the refined reference must beat 'k' by at least 0.05 registered AUC (2 seeds x 6 evaluations).

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Consolidate contacts in the object frame and gate them by wrench feasibility. Take the medoid of each stable contact run per manipulation segment (sidedness test included). Solve min ||G lambda - w_req||^2 subject to friction cones, with a table support disc. Reject hovering contacts and add thumb-finger opposition where lifts need it.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: C2Dex https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07045 (verified); DexForge contactaware.yaml (code read: 10 mm gate, 8-frame minimum, 80 % stable fraction); EgoCPT https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17572 (verified HTML: force allocation over candidate contacts).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: We snap per frame from fingertips with 1-2 cm noise and a 25 mm gate. Consolidation was worth +40 pp end-to-end in C2Dex, and force allocation took EgoCPT from 1/10 to 10/10.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 1 day on CPU. Risks: the kit's 0.3 kg placeholder mass makes w_req uncertain; normal noise on thin boards.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Two thresholds. If fewer than 60 % of ep24/ep18 contact frames fall into consistent runs (80 % of points within 8 mm of the medoid), consolidation does not apply. If the NNLS residual exceeds 20 % of ||w_req|| on most ep24 lift frames even after promoting weaker contacts, the contact evidence does not support a two-hand lift. If both pass, an RL A/B against 'k' must gain at least 0.03 on a hard episode.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Grip preload: in consolidated contact segments, command pad targets 2-4 mm INSIDE the surface instead of 1 mm outside, so that PD tracking produces normal force. Keep frame 0 and other reset frames clean.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: ContactOpt https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07267 (verified: deliberately allows interpenetration to stand in for soft tissue). OATH https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14379 (verified, abstract): tracking the kinematic position alone does not induce contact forces.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: contact_retarget pushes every hand to +1 mm clearance, so the reference never squeezes. This may explain why penetration fell 3-4x while the mean AUC barely moved (ep27 -0.031).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Hours (a flag in contact_retarget). Risk: reset pops if preloaded frames are used as resets without the assist; exclude them or keep the assist on in training.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: CPU stiff-wrist replay without a policy, object free: with preload, the carried object follows through ep12 and ep24 carry segments for clearly more frames than without. If the frame counts are equal, drop the idea. Otherwise A/B on GPU (ep12, ep24; 2 seeds x 6 evaluations).

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Whole-trajectory spacetime retargeting with analytic Jacobians, in place of forward per-frame LM. Solve both hands jointly, with contact persistence in the object frame, velocity and acceleration costs, and collisions on Sharpa primitive capsules against our convex pieces.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: PyRoki examples/09 and 11 hand retargeting (code read: trajectory-level contact costs). Gleicher 1998 spacetime retargeting and footskate cleanup (search only). DexForge temporal operator (code read: trajectory_smoothing_seconds 0.1).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Our sequential solve (left hand first, then the right, which sees the left) cannot trade off future frames, and it re-snaps targets every frame. A joint solve removes the jitter and the asymmetric hand-hand bias.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-3 days. Risk: the JAX geometry loses exact evaluator collision. Keep MjPen as a post-check.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Required: lower contact slip in the object frame and lower jerk, with no rise in the pop map. If registered AUC changes by less than 0.02 on all 4 validation episodes (2 seeds x 6 evaluations), it is not worth keeping.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Self-generated reference flywheel: replace hard segments of the reference with the robot trajectory actually achieved by the best existing policy, chosen without ground truth (lowest per-frame sim_vs_ref error). Then retrain with resets on those physically valid states.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: DexTrack https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09614 (verified: data flywheel and homotopy optimisation). Gen2Dex https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24392 (verified: cache of physically valid reset states). PhysDiff https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02500 (verified: physics projection between denoising steps). Iterative learning control as an analogy.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Achieved states are physically valid by construction and cost no new solver.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 1 extra training per episode (estimated $3 each at overnight rates). Risk: it locks in the policy's failures. Splice only segments where the rollout tracks our reference.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: If the second-iteration policy's registered AUC is at or below the first's on 3 of 4 episodes, the idea is falsified.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Morphology-matched hand before IK. Replace the uniform 1.2x scale about the wrist with per-segment ratios to the Sharpa's link lengths (palm and each finger), then re-pose so the human contact points are kept, before E2S.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Morphometric Imitation https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28660 (verified: up to +35 pp downstream success; Sharpa real-world 89.3 %). OmniRetarget (verified): scaling hand keypoints drives the robot hand into the object.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The uniform scale is the documented cause of the 16-20 mm robot penetration that contact_retarget later fights with a bounded wrist.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 1 day. Risk: only 21 joints and no MANO surface, so the contact recovery is coarse.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: If E2S with morphometric scaling does not reduce p95 robot penetration below the current 16-20 mm, or the share of start frames that pop, on the 4 episodes, drop it.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Synthesise fingers from object motion for non-prehensile phases. Copy only the wrist (and possibly the contact side) from the human. Let a contact-invariant or contact-sampling planner, or MuJoCo MPC predictive sampling, find finger contacts that move the board as perceived (slide to the edge, pivot, lift).
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Ye and Liu, Synthesis of Detailed Hand Manipulations Using Contact Sampling, SIGGRAPH 2012 (search only: input is object and body mocap, output is physically plausible finger motion). Mordatch, Popovic and Todorov, Contact-Invariant Optimization for Hand Manipulation, SCA 2012 (search only). MJPC https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.00541 (verified).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Our object trajectory is the most reliable signal (reference vs mocap 0.80-0.98), while human fingertips hover 1.8 cm off the board on ep24. Extrinsic-dexterity phases are where finger copying fails.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 3-5 days, research-level risk. MJPC runs in MuJoCo, not Newton, so plans need re-validation in FlashCHORD.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Time box of 1 day: if the planner cannot reproduce ep24 board 2's stand-up in simulation with a Sharpa hand, abandon it.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Object-centric reference with a weak finger prior: lower or remove finger-joint tracking in the FlashCHORD reward. Keep the wrist, object and contact terms, using a one-sided fingertip distance (unsigned reference distance, so the robot may close gaps).
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: ObjDex https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04005 (verified: wrist from a generative prior, fingers learned by RL). FlashDexRetarget https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01849 (verified: Sharpa, multi-reference RL). DexMachina's virtual object controllers (verified).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The human finger configuration mapped onto the Sharpa is the least trustworthy part of our reference, yet it is tracked densely.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Config or reward change plus a GPU A/B (about $6-8 per pair, estimate). Risk: slower learning; may hurt the easy episodes.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: A/B on ep24 and ep18 against 'k' (2 seeds x 6 evaluations), plus ep12 as a control. Falsified if neither hard episode gains at least 0.03, or if ep12 loses more than 0.03.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Decide contacts and the touched side from stereo-depth occlusion order rather than fingertip proximity alone: compare measured hand depth with the object depth rendered from our mesh and track, inside the hand mask.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: OmniHOI's occlusion-order loss on rendered hand and object depth (verified HTML mentions occlusion-aware reconstruction; per the repo review). EgoCPT treats video contacts as uncertain (verified).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: It fixes wrong-face snaps on thin boards and hovering fingertips, which the 25 mm gate accepts.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 1 day on CPU. Risk: depth noise around 1 cm at object edges.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On public episodes, as a diagnostic only, after inference: compare per-finger contact and side against contacts derived from mocap. If agreement is not better than our geometric gate, drop it.

stage: Stages 5-6: RL tracking policy training (FlashCHORD/FlashSAC), choosing checkpoints and variants without ground truth, repeat evaluation, QA gates. Summary: little of this is innovative. Training is the organisers' recipe run as is, plus two opt-in patches ported from other recipes; neither moved the score beyond noise. Selection is standard practice: pick by tracking error against our own reference, which papers in this subfield already do. The careful part is the engineering. We checked that the GT-free proxy actually tracks the true score, and we run physics probes in the evaluator's own physics before spending GPU money. Measured in this review from the 132 committed rollouts (results/e2e/overnight_20261022/**/summary.json and selection.json, read only): sim_vs_ref vs registered AUC, policy-mean Spearman 0.98 on ep18 (9 policies), 0.86 on ep24 (7 policies, all within 0.04), 1.0 on ep12 and ep27 (3 each). Rollout-level Spearman: 0.95, 0.86, 0.73 and 0.93 on ep12, ep18, ep24 and ep27. The single-rollout checkpoint sweep scores its chosen checkpoint +0.026 above that checkpoint's own 6-evaluation mean (average over 17 runs; range -0.001 to +0.083), so part of each choice is noise. Compared with the literature, we are missing: an adaptive or gated assist curriculum, failure-weighted or backward resets, domain randomisation, a teacher-student or MPC teacher, repeated evaluations inside the sweep, and more than one seed per variant.

components.component: Per-episode RL tracking policy (FlashCHORD + FlashSAC)
components.what_we_do:
pipeline_ep.sh stage 4: scripts/train_flash_sac.py experiment=sharpa_flash_sac on one episode's reference, 250,003,456 env steps, seed 42 (43 for a few runs), motion_speed 1.0, 4,096 worlds, logging disabled. Upstream recipe unchanged (docs/research/notes/01-baseline-dissection.md):
- 56-D residual action on the reference: 5 cm / 0.15 rad / 0.15 rad, EMA 0.3, soft wrist kp 25.
- Reward: object keypoints w20, contact-wrench support w10, hand terms 0.25.
- Fixed 11-stage VOC object-assist schedule, assist 0 from 122.9M steps.
- Reset: uniform frame, fingers opened U(0, 0.7), 20-step assisted hold.
- Instant terminations: object 10 cm / 0.5 rad, palm 15 cm.
- No domain randomisation.
Evaluated with the official evaluate_policy.py: reset_mode=explicit, 1 world, assist 0.
components.closest_prior_art:
- CHORD, arXiv 2607.00033 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00033). Verified: abstract and HTML opened (Tables 1-2, §4.3).
- DexMachina, arXiv 2505.24853 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24853): VOC with decaying strength. Verified: abstract and HTML Alg. 1.
- FlashCHORD is the organisers' implementation of the two.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing in the learner. Only the reference it is fed is ours (stages 1-4).
components.evidence_it_matters:
Registered AUC with our meshes, 6 evaluations each (docs/overnight-2026-10-22.md):
- ep27 0.942 ± 0.017
- ep12 0.725 ± 0.067
- ep18 0.345 ± 0.046 → 0.715 ± 0.240 once the mesh could stand
- ep24 0.297 ± 0.055
Every ep24 variant lands at 0.28-0.32: the policy never learns to lift a board and stand it on its edge. Reference vs mocap is 0.98 on ep18 and 0.80 on ep24, so on the hard episodes the learner, not perception, loses most of the score.

components.component: Deployment-exact start patch (FC_IMMEDIATE_FIRST_FRAME)
components.what_we_do: ops/box/patch_flashchord.py edits lifecycle/reset.py (warp kernel). Once curriculum VOC < first_frame_voc_threshold (0.1), a fraction p of resets (0.25 in our runs) become evaluation-like: frame 0, finger factor 1, no 20-step hold, current curriculum assist. Opt-in by env var; unset means upstream behaviour. The docstring says it is modelled on NVIDIA's ReconBody humanoid reset (25 % then 50 % immediate starts).
components.closest_prior_art:
- DeepMimic reference state initialisation and early termination, arXiv 1804.02717 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02717). Verified: ar5iv opened; RSI and ET are reported as critical.
- NVIDIA's ReconBody reset inside FlashCHORD. Only our patch docstring states this; the FlashCHORD source was not reopened in this review.
- FDR resets with ~1 mm / 1° noise and no hold. Verified in a clone of github.com/Holiday-Robot/FlashDexRetarget (config/envs/commands).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: A port of a reset NVIDIA already uses elsewhere to the Sharpa reset. It closes a real train/eval mismatch, but nothing about it is new.
components.evidence_it_matters:
No consistent effect, one seed, 6 evaluations:
- ep24: 0.318 ± 0.001 vs 0.307 ± 0.002
- ep18: 0.342 ± 0.096 vs 0.319 ± 0.042
- ep12: 0.763 vs 0.790
- ep27: 0.897 vs 0.911
Not adopted.

components.component: Object-keypoint scale patch (FC_OBJECT_KEYPOINT_SCALE)
components.what_we_do: Multiplies FlashCHORD's six ±1 m object-axis keypoints by a scalar (0.15 in run kq), so rotation no longer dominates the object reward. Training reward only; observations, terminations and the evaluator are unchanged.
components.closest_prior_art: FlashDexRetarget, arXiv 2610.01849 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01849): 128 object surface points rescaled so the max radius is 5.8 cm, error = mean of the top-3 point distances. Verified: abstract and HTML opened. Reward details are from our docs/research/port-recipes-2026-10-21.md (code read on 2026-10-21).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: A one-line, cruder version of FDR's object-scaled point reward: a uniform scale, not per object, and the reward kernel is unchanged.
components.evidence_it_matters:
One seed, within noise:
- ep18: 0.381 ± 0.012 (k s42 0.319, s43 0.361)
- ep24: 0.313 ± 0.011 vs 0.307
Tightest spread on both. Not adopted.

components.component: Embodiment variants for training (primitive-collision hand, mid-stiffness wrist)
components.what_we_do:
- NVIDIA's sharpa_hands_primitive (24 collision primitives per hand), switched by a config line.
- Our flashchord_conf/embodiment/sharpa_hands_mid.yaml: wrist kp 400 vs 25.
Both trained with the same recipe.
components.closest_prior_art:
- NVIDIA ships sharpa_hands_primitive in FlashCHORD (observed in our CPU tests; no paper).
- DexMachina uses its benchmark to compare hand hardware designs (abstract verified).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing. These are config choices.
components.evidence_it_matters:
- Mid wrist falsified on both hard episodes: ep18 0.193 vs 0.381, ep24 0.050 vs 0.096 (single rollouts, 2026-10-21).
- Primitive hand: ep18 0.377 ± 0.021, ep24 0.282 ± 0.023 (6 evaluations).
Neither adopted.

components.component: Checkpoint sweep chosen by sim_vs_ref (no ground truth)
components.what_we_do:
pipeline_ep.sh 5b with CK_SWEEP='0.4 0.6 0.8':
- Candidates: the saved checkpoints nearest 100/150/200M plus the final 250M; one official-evaluator rollout each.
- Score: qa.py policy. Kit AUC functions (_warp_to_reference_start, _object_add, _add_auc) between the simulated and the reference object poses stored in the evaluator parquet, using 500 points on a 5 cm sphere per object (no mesh).
- Rule: keep the maximum; selection.json records it.
Observed choices over 17 runs: final 8, 200M 5, 150M 2, 100M 2.
components.closest_prior_art:
- DexMachina App. B.4: 5 seeds; each run saves a best checkpoint by cumulative task reward, evaluated over 20 episodes against the demonstration. Verified: HTML opened.
- robomimic, arXiv 2108.03298 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.03298) §C4: evaluates every checkpoint online and reports the best per run; final and lowest-validation-loss checkpoints lose performance. Verified: ar5iv opened.
- FDR: periodic deterministic evaluation that archives the first rollout per clip passing the success criterion against the reference. Verified in the clone (src/evaluation/evaluate.py, callbacks/success_export.py).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Ground truth is not needed because the selection target is our own reference, which the robomimic/DexMachina recipe already allows. Our version is weaker than theirs: one rollout per candidate (they use 20 episodes) and only four candidates.
components.evidence_it_matters: Computed in this review from 17 selection.json files vs the 6-evaluation summaries of the same checkpoints: the sweep's score for its chosen checkpoint exceeds that checkpoint's own 6-evaluation mean by +0.026 on average (-0.001 to +0.083; ep18 kfi 0.816 vs 0.733). This is winner's curse: part of the choice is noise. Unknown: whether a non-chosen checkpoint has a higher mean, because those were never evaluated repeatedly. Earlier measurement: the same ep18 100M checkpoint scored 0.308 in one evaluation and 0.192 in another.

components.component: Selection among reference variants and seeds, with automatic retries (auto_ep.sh, overnight recommendation)
components.what_we_do:
1. qa.py ref ranks candidate references: robot wrist IK p95 ≤ 60 mm and max wrist step ≤ 10 cm, else +1000 penalty.
2. Train the best-ranked one.
3. If the verdict is not 'ok', train the other variant, then seed+1 (RETRIES ≤ 2).
4. Publish the attempt with the highest sim_vs_ref, with the checkpoint's sha256.
Overnight recommendation: per episode, train E2S, contact-retargeted and rest-settled references and keep the best by mean sim_vs_ref. Valid because only the robot hand differs between variants: the object target comes from perception, so the yardstick is the same for all of them.
components.closest_prior_art:
- Paine et al. 2020, Hyperparameter Selection for Offline RL, arXiv 2007.09055 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.09055). Title verified; content from search summary.
- Pessimistic Model Selection for offline DRL, arXiv 2111.14346 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14346). Abstract verified.
- FDR retargeting: up to 6 attempts per clip, keep the one minimising tip error + 0.5 × penetration (from our port-recipes doc; only the quality-flag block of that config was re-verified here).
- Successive halving / Hyperband, arXiv 1603.06560 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06560). Title verified.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Treating whole reference pipelines as hyperparameters chosen by the shared object yardstick is sensible engineering, not a new method. The retry tree is a hand-written heuristic: not a bandit or racing scheme, and no confidence intervals.
components.evidence_it_matters: Policy-mean rank agreement with registered AUC (this review): ep18 Spearman 0.98 over 9 policies; ep24 0.86 over 7 (all within 0.04 of each other); ep12 and ep27 1.0 over 3 each. Overnight: sim_vs_ref ranked base vs retargeting like the true score on all four episodes (one tie). Choosing by it keeps retargeting's ep12 gain (+0.066) and avoids its ep27 loss (-0.031).

components.component: Repeat-evaluation protocol
components.what_we_do:
hard_ab.sh evalrep:
- NREP = 6 official evaluations (3 in parallel) of a chosen checkpoint.
- Each scored by sim_vs_ref and by score_registered.py (kit registered scorer, our meshes, public scan as stand-in).
- Reports mean, std, min, max and the AUC of the best-by-sim_vs_ref rollout.
Seeds: mostly one per variant (s43 for a few). Rule written in the docs: at least 2 seeds × 6 evaluations per decision. No confidence intervals, no paired tests.
components.closest_prior_art:
- Colas et al., How Many Random Seeds?, arXiv 1806.08295 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.08295). Abstract verified.
- Agarwal et al., Deep RL at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice, NeurIPS 2021 (rliable: IQM, stratified bootstrap CIs). Search results only, not opened.
- DexMachina: 5 seeds × 20 evaluation episodes (verified).
- CHORD: 3 seeds per task (verified, Table 1).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: The repeats measure GPU-simulator nondeterminism of an evaluator the kit calls deterministic (seed 42). That matters if the organisers re-run policies. Our statistics are below the field's norm in seeds.
components.evidence_it_matters:
- One policy's spread: ±0.001 (ep24 ki) to ±0.240 (ep18 kfi: rollouts 0.18-0.84).
- Seed-to-seed: ≈0.04.
- The 2026-10-21 single-rollout scores were low draws (ep24 0.232 vs 0.297 mean).

components.component: Policy QA verdict against the static floor (qa.py policy)
components.what_we_do:
Computes sim_vs_ref and the floor (the reference's objects held at their frame-0 poses, scored against the reference). Verdicts:
- harmful: sim < floor
- weak: sim < max(floor + 0.05, 0.5)
- ok: otherwise
The verdict drives auto_ep.sh retries.
components.closest_prior_art: A do-nothing or zero-action baseline is generic practice; no specific paper. The success thresholds used elsewhere (SPIDER-style 10 cm / 0.5 rad; CHORD 15 cm / 40°) are the closest formal analogue (CHORD verified).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: For an object-only metric it is a useful gate. It showed that on ep18 the trained policy scored below doing nothing (0.40 vs floor 0.64).
components.evidence_it_matters: It flagged ep18 and ep24 as harmful or weak on 2026-10-21 and drove the retries. The thresholds have not been calibrated against outcomes.

components.component: Physics QA probes and drop tests before GPU training
components.closest_prior_art:
- Gen2Dex, arXiv 2610.24392 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24392): cache of physically valid reset states validated in simulation. Its Table IV: raw-reference resets solve 0/10 tasks vs 9/10 with valid states. Verified: HTML opened.
- FDR retargeting quality flags: palm acceleration 60 m/s², tip error > 3 cm on > 35 % of frames, penetration 2 cm. Verified in the clone (config/retarget/kinematic_retargeting.yaml).
- Do as I Do (arXiv 2606.19333): welded warm-up and base plates for unstable objects. Abstract verified; details from our port-recipes doc.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: The same idea as validated resets, run in the official evaluator's own physics with the exact evaluation start conditions (assist off, exact fingers, no hold), as a cheap pre-GPU diagnostic. Its output is not yet used to change training: no reset filter or weighting.
components.evidence_it_matters:
- Found objects that drop or fall with no hand near them in 3 of 4 references (ep12 cup tips 23° in 4 steps; ep18 sweeper 17.6° by step 4; ep27 and ep12 racks drop ~1 cm).
- Found ep24's reset hand overlap (fixed: 0.080 → 0.232).
- Diagnosed the ep18 mesh flaw whose fix gave 0.345 → 0.715 (5 of 6 rollouts 0.79-0.84).

components.component: Best-of-N rollout selection at test time (considered, not adopted)
components.what_we_do: Pick, among N official-evaluator rollouts of one checkpoint, the rollout with the highest sim_vs_ref. Left to the owner because of rule risk: it cherry-picks stochastic rollouts, and the organisers may re-run.
components.closest_prior_art: Verifier-ranked best-of-N sampling (generic). Sampling MPC in SPIDER (arXiv 2511.09484, verified) chooses among sampled rollouts, but as a planner, not after the fact.
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Nothing. The open question is whether it is allowed.
components.evidence_it_matters: Best-of-6 by sim_vs_ref minus the 6-evaluation mean (this review, 22 policies): -0.013 to +0.127; median ≈ +0.014; ep18 base +0.056; ep24 mostly ≈ 0. Earlier ep18 test: +0.08.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Failure-weighted reset sampling, seeded by our clean-start map. Bin the reference frames; sample start frames in proportion to the smoothed termination/failure rate per bin plus a uniform floor (BeyondMimic). Exclude or down-weight start frames that frame_quality_probe marks as physically unclean.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: FlashCHORD samples start frames uniformly, so ep24's short lift-and-stand segments (board 1 ~f102, board 2 ~f117), where every variant fails, get few training starts. BeyondMimic reports that long sequences never converged without adaptive sampling.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep24 (and ep18 kfi), 2 seeds × 6 evaluations, 250M steps. Falsified if mean registered AUC < 0.37 (+0.05 over 0.318), or no rollout lifts board 1 past f102 within 5 cm, or ep12/ep27 controls regress > 0.02.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- BeyondMimic, arXiv 2508.08241 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.08241): adaptive sampling with a uniform floor of 0.1/S and a non-causal ρ=0.8 kernel. Verified in the HTML.
- Prioritized Level Replay, arXiv 2010.03934 (abstract verified).
- PHC hard-negative mining, arXiv 2305.06456 (verified, ar5iv).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 60-100 lines in reset.py (per-bin counters in warp) plus 2 trainings per episode, ≈ $5 per episode at ≈ $2.4 per policy. Risk: forgetting the easy segments; the uniform floor mitigates it.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Backward curriculum over valid reset states. Start training near the end of the episode and move the start earlier as success rises. Use only resets that pass the physics probe (contact-retargeted and rest-settled states).
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Gen2Dex's ablation (10 tasks) solves 9/10 with valid states + backward starts, vs 5/10 with random frames and 0/10 with raw reference states. Our references are video-derived and imperfect, the same regime.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Same protocol as the reset-sampling idea on ep24 and ep18. Falsified if the gain is < 0.05 and below the failure-weighted sampler's.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- Gen2Dex, arXiv 2610.24392 (verified, Table IV).
- Reverse Curriculum Generation, arXiv 1707.05300 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.05300; abstract verified).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Reset patch plus a success-gated schedule; 2 trainings per episode. Risk: interaction with FlashCHORD's fixed assist schedule, and the late frames of ep24 may be unclean too.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Performance-gated assist decay with dial-back instead of the fixed 11-stage schedule. Decay the VOC gains only when the running task-reward and completion means exceed thresholds; restore gains if completion collapses.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Our assist reaches 0 at 122.9M whether or not the policy has learned to take over. CHORD itself states the contact reward must converge before the assist decays. On 2026-10-21 both first runs picked the checkpoint right after the assist ended.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep24 and ep18 kfi, 2 seeds × 6 evaluations. Falsified if mean AUC gain < 0.05 or ep12/ep27 regress > 0.02. Log the step at which the assist reaches 0 (logging is currently off).
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- DexMachina Algorithm 1, arXiv 2505.24853 (verified, HTML).
- FDR xfrc_curriculum_adaptive: completion threshold 0.65, dial-back at 0.5 after 500 epochs. Verified in the clone (config/envs/curriculum/flashdexretarget.yaml).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About 1 day to port into the FlashCHORD curriculum; ≈ $10 for the test. Risk: the assist may never fully release on ep24 within 250M steps, so a hard deadline is needed.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Self-imitation / success recycling. Fine-tune the policy on its own successful rollouts (top sim_vs_ref rollouts as a BC term or a replay prefill). This turns stochastic 'best-of-N' luck into one checkpoint with a higher mean and less spread.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: ep18 kfi already succeeds in 5 of 6 rollouts (0.79-0.84) but has one 0.18 failure. The submitted run is a single draw, so cutting the failure rate is worth more than raising the best case. It also gets the gain of best-of-N (rule-risky) by a legitimate route.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep18 kfi: fine-tune 25-50M steps. Falsified if, over 12 evaluations, mean AUC ≤ 0.75 or the share of rollouts < 0.5 is not lower than 1/6.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- Self-Imitation Learning, arXiv 1806.05635 (abstract verified).
- DexTrack data flywheel, arXiv 2502.09614 (abstract verified).
- DONIC, arXiv 2610.29997: 'recycles verified successful executions into training demonstrations' (abstract verified).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Needs a BC loss or buffer-prefill hook in FlashSAC (about 1 day) plus ≈ $2 per test. Risk: overfitting to noise-specific trajectories; mitigated because the rollouts come from the same simulator.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Replicated, risk-aware checkpoint selection. After the assist reaches 0, evaluate every kept checkpoint (≈ every 25-50M steps) with 3-6 rollouts; choose by mean − 1 sd or the second-worst rollout, not by one draw. Use successive halving to spend the extra evaluations only on contenders.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Measured: the single-rollout sweep scores its chosen checkpoint +0.026 above that checkpoint's own mean (up to +0.083). Spreads reach ±0.24, and the organisers' run is one draw, so the lower tail is what costs us.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Re-evaluate the 100/150/200/250M checkpoints of 4 existing runs (ep18 mck s42/s43, ep24 mcsk s42/s43; all in the HF store) 6 times each. Falsified if the replicated rule picks the same checkpoint as the sweep in ≥ 3/4 runs, or improves the chosen 6-evaluation mean by < 0.01.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- Pessimistic Model Selection, arXiv 2111.14346 (abstract verified).
- rliable / Agarwal 2021 (search results only).
- Hyperband, arXiv 1603.06560 (title verified).
- DexMachina's 20-episode checkpoint evaluation (verified).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Evaluations only: ≈ 1 GPU-h for the test, ≈ +20-30 min per episode in production. Low risk.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Weight averaging (SWA, EMA or a 'policy soup') of the actor weights from the last few checkpoints of one run, submitted as a single checkpoint.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Averaging nearby checkpoints often lands in a flatter optimum, with less sensitivity to small state differences. That could cut the GPU-nondeterminism spread we measure, at zero training cost.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Average the actors of 200/225/250M (or an EMA) for ep12 k, ep18 kfi and ep24 ki; 6 evaluations each. Falsified if the mean < the best constituent's mean − 0.01 and the std is not lower.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- Model soups, arXiv 2203.05482 (abstract verified).
- SWA, arXiv 1803.05407 (title verified).
- Nikishin et al. 2018 (SWA for DDPG): known only from a secondary citation, not verified.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: CPU averaging of safetensors plus evaluations, < $1. Risk: SAC actors at different stages may not average well (weight-space interpolation is not guaranteed along an RL run); FlashSAC normalisation statistics must be handled.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Light domain randomisation and perturbations in training: object mass and friction around the kit's 0.3 kg placeholder; ~1 cm / 2° start noise; small external wrenches on held, lifted objects.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: FlashCHORD trains with no randomisation, yet the evaluation itself varies between rollouts (GPU nondeterminism), and our meshes and masses are approximate. Robust policies should have tighter spreads and degrade less under contact noise.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep18 kfi and ep12 k, 2 seeds × 6 evaluations. Falsified if the 6-evaluation std does not drop by ≥ 30 % or the mean falls by > 0.02.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- OpenAI Dactyl, arXiv 1808.00177 (abstract verified).
- Do as I Do perturbation ablation (from our port-recipes doc, not reopened).
- Morphometric Imitation, arXiv 2609.28660 (title verified; DR list from port-recipes).
- BeyondMimic warns that excessive randomisation makes behaviour conservative (verified, HTML).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Moderate patching of the scene and reset; ≈ $5-10. Risk: slower learning on the hard episodes.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Scale the learner: critic 1024 wide and a 50M-transition replay buffer (FDR), and/or 500M steps on the hard episodes.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: In FDR's ablation on the same hand with FlashSAC, success rose 34 % → 60 % (buffer) → 86 % (critic). That was multi-reference, so for one episode this is a hypothesis.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep24 and ep18 kfi, 2 seeds × 6 evaluations at equal wall-clock. Falsified if the gain is < 0.05.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: FlashDexRetarget §IV-C, arXiv 2610.01849 (verified, HTML).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Config changes if FlashCHORD exposes them. FDR's buffer needs ≈ 88 GB host RAM for 50M fp16 (from port-recipes), so use 10-20M. Slower steps: ≈ $5-10.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Iterative learning control on the reference. Treat each episode as a repeated task: after a training round, shift the robot-hand part of the reference (the feedforward the residual policy builds on) by −K × the per-frame object or wrist tracking error seen in rollouts, then fine-tune. The object target never changes; no ground truth is used.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Our policy is residual around a kinematic reference with ±5 cm / 0.15 rad authority and a soft wrist (kp 25). Systematic lags and offsets the residual cannot absorb can be moved into the reference, which is what ILC does for repeated trajectories.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep24 and ep12: one ILC iteration + 50M fine-tuning steps. Falsified if mean sim_vs_ref over 6 evaluations improves by < 0.03 vs the pre-ILC policy, or the registered AUC does not move with it.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- IRLC/I2RLC, arXiv 2604.16850: updates an impedance controller's reference from observed tracking errors (abstract verified).
- Bristow, Tharayil & Alleyne 2006 ILC survey, IEEE CSM 26(3) (search result only).
- Search for ILC combined with residual RL for dexterous tracking found nothing beyond these; my own hypothesis.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: CPU script plus fine-tuning, ≈ $2 per iteration per episode. Risk: correcting the hands can break contacts; errors from contact-rich segments may not be correctable by feedforward alone.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: An MPC teacher for the policy: generate a dynamically feasible robot trajectory with batched sampling MPC (SPIDER / Do as I Do style, annealed contact guidance) for the hard segments. Use it as the reference, or as a BC/DAgger teacher for the FlashCHORD policy.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: SPIDER reports that a policy trained from its physics-feasible reference completes the task (0.99 ± 0.01 progress over 7 seeds) where the kinematic-reference policy stalls (0.07 ± 0.11). ep24's board stand-up is exactly where our kinematic references fail.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Without any policy: falsified if the MPC alone cannot move ep24 board 1 through its lift (f95-f125) within 5 cm / 0.5 rad of our reference with the assist off.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- SPIDER, arXiv 2511.09484 (verified, HTML §4.2.1).
- Do as I Do, arXiv 2606.19333 (abstract verified).
- Our forensics doc (idea D).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-4 days of engineering (the Do as I Do repo has a Sharpa option per our notes). Before Nov 4 this is the most expensive idea here. Risk: MuJoCo-Warp vs Newton physics mismatch.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: A better no-GT proxy: score rollouts against our reference using our own reconstructed meshes with the registered-scorer pipeline (and per-object SP/MP) instead of 500 points on a 5 cm sphere.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The sphere ignores object size, so it under-weights rotation errors of large or thin objects (boards, sweeper) relative to the real ADD. At rollout level, our proxy's Spearman with the true score is only 0.73 on ep24 and 0.86 on ep18.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Recompute both proxies on the 132 existing rollouts (parquets in the HF store, CPU only). Falsified if the within-episode Spearman with registered AUC does not rise above 0.73 (ep24) and 0.86 (ep18).
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: SIMPLER, arXiv 2405.05941: validate an evaluation proxy by its correlation with the real metric (abstract verified). Integrity: our meshes and references are inference-time data.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Hours of CPU, no GPU. Low risk. It cannot remove perception error, which is shared by every variant of an episode.

out_of_box_ideas.idea: A single multi-reference policy (FDR / DONIC style) trained over all public and eval references of the same object sets, instead of 20 independent per-episode policies.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Skills such as board lifting would be shared between public ep23/ep24 and their eval twins. FDR converts 90 % of 50 clips in about 30 GPU-h, vs about 3,000 GPU-h for CHORD (PPO).
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Train on 19 public episodes, hold out 1 hard and 1 easy episode. Falsified if the held-in hard episodes do not beat per-episode policies at equal total GPU-h, or the easy ones lose > 0.03.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy:
- FlashDexRetarget, arXiv 2610.01849 (verified).
- DONIC, arXiv 2610.29997 (abstract verified).
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: High: FlashCHORD would need multi-reference support. The output must still be a FlashCHORD checkpoint, and the 2026-11-04 freeze leaves little time. Not before the first full submission.

stage: How new is the whole V2D Track 3 approach (repo commit 2284dbf, 2026-10-22) compared with 2025-26 research, the two leading teams and NVIDIA? VERDICT: none of our components is new. The approach is a well-measured, carefully engineered version of the field's standard recipe: reconstruct the scene, retarget the hands, then train RL per episode. This is the organisers' own CHORD route, and RoboWheel, Do as I Do, EgoMatrix, OmniHOI and C2Dex follow it too. After a real search, nothing qualifies as 'novel'. What is original sits in combinations fitted to this scorer: (a) fusing meshes per object across episodes from stereo, where hand, table and other-object pixels only clear space and never add surface; (b) contact retargeting checked against the training simulator's exact collision model; (c) mesh and pose fixes triggered by tests that run the simulator with the training-only object assist switched off (as in the official evaluation). The interaction-aware mesh idea, not yet built, would be a genuine new combination; its closest precedents are Vysics (RSS 2025) and Picasso (RSS 2026). AHEAD of NVIDIA's Track 3 starter pipeline: we use stereo depth instead of single-camera depth, track several objects, build our own meshes, and choose between variants without ground truth. LEVEL with the likely leaders on perception: FoundationPose plus stereo is the obvious NVIDIA-toolchain choice. BEHIND on mesh accuracy: our CD-O is 0.3-0.6 cm against SoySauceChicken's 0.065 cm. On the leaderboard pulled 2026-10-22 05:31 UTC, three teams cluster at 0.065-0.088 cm, and two of them score only 0.42 and 0.53 AUC. My inference is that 0.065 is the level of near-exact or scan-like meshes, not better reconstruction. Zihao Guo's 0.313 cm matches ours. CLEARLY BEHIND on policy success in the hard episodes: Guo succeeds on 19 of 20 episodes (SP-SR 0.95), while our ep24 sits at 0.31. Our 4-episode mean is 0.58-0.68; theirs is 0.83-0.85. Corrections to the brief: the default perception script perc2.py does not use OWLv2 (its docstring is stale). Detection is SAM2 masks matched to DINOv2 renders of the mesh (CNOS-style). Also, the mesh library was built from public-episode tracks made with the public scans, an owner-approved development aid ('A-lite'). The challenge page could not be opened today (DNS failure), so rule statements rest on the repo's notes.

components.component: 0. Overall architecture
components.what_we_do: An open-loop chain. Stereo perception produces object tracks; we build our own meshes; MediaPipe hands are lifted to 3-D with stereo depth. The organisers' E2S inverse kinematics maps them to the Sharpa hand, then a CPU contact-retargeting step and rest settling follow. FlashCHORD/FlashSAC trains one policy per episode from scratch (250M steps). The official evaluator runs it, and we choose among variants by sim_vs_ref: the rollout scored against our own reference, no ground truth. Physics enters only in RL, plus CPU drop and replay probes.
components.closest_prior_art: CHORD https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00033 (opened). NVIDIA video_to_data end-to-end workflow https://github.com/nvidia-isaac/video_to_data (README opened). RoboWheel https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02729 (opened). Do as I Do https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19333 (opened). EgoMatrix https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18822 (opened). OmniHOI https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10855 (opened). C2Dex https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07045 (opened). V2P-Manip https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16436 (opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Same overall pattern as the organisers and every 2026 video-to-dexterous paper. Different from NVIDIA's Track 3 starter pipeline: stereo, several objects, own meshes, choosing variants without ground truth. Behind current research in two ways: no physics-in-the-loop refinement of the reference (SPIDER, Do as I Do, OmniHOI, DexForge), and no multi-reference RL (FlashDexRetarget). Inference about the leaders: both probably run the same skeleton, so the gap is execution quality, not architecture.
components.evidence_it_matters: Mean over 4 validation episodes (6 evaluations each): 0.577 for the base, 0.587 with contact retargeting; best per episode about 0.68 with ep18 at 0.715. Leaders: 0.848 and 0.831.

components.component: 1. Perception (perc2.py)
components.what_we_do: Depth: rectify the mono stereo pair (c/b) and run FoundationStereo (scale 0.5, 32 iterations), cached. Frame-0 detection: SAM2 automatic masks are matched by DINOv2 ViT-L descriptors against 42 grey nvdiffrast renders of each mesh (CNOS-style), with an intensity term and a 3-D size gate (0.3-1.3 times the mesh extent). Hungarian assignment, then the default 'compact' joint prior penalises a spread of the chosen 3-D centroids beyond 0.45 m. This path does not use OWLv2, contrary to the docstrings. Tracking: FoundationPose register (5 iterations) then track_one (2 iterations) per object, with grey textures. Camera motion: keyframe SIFT (4000 features) plus depth-backprojected PnP-RANSAC (SQPnP, LM refinement); new keyframe below 250 inliers; world frame = rectified-left camera at frame 0.
components.closest_prior_art: CNOS https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.11067 (opened). FoundationPose https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08344 (opened). FoundationStereo https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09898 (opened). NVIDIA's reconstruction modules (FoundationStereo, FoundationPose, cuSFM, BundleSDF, multi-view HOI) https://github.com/nvidia-isaac/video_to_data/tree/main/reconstruction (README opened). RoboWheel (FoundationPose on a generated mesh plus DROID-SLAM) https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02729 (abstract opened; details from repo notes). Hand2Robot (globally consistent trajectory chosen from per-frame candidates) https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15769 (opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Off-the-shelf models in a composition that is NVIDIA's own stack (all Bowen Wen tools). Small dataset-specific adaptations: the compactness prior and the 3-D size gate. Ahead of the Track 3 starter pipeline (MoGe single-camera depth, one object, DROID-SLAM); probably the same as the leaders. Behind current research on robustness: no re-registration or track recovery, no selection of a globally consistent trajectory among pose candidates, no loop closure. The room-map and marker ideas from the professor package are not in the code path.
components.evidence_it_matters: Compactness prior: 20-episode mean AUC 0.883 to 0.932 (public scans as meshes); ep26 0.065 to 0.988. Our references against mocap: ep18 0.98, ep24 0.80-0.84. Tracking with our own meshes on 8 public episodes (the 'H2' check) has not been run yet.

components.component: 2. Hands (hands_mp.py, hand_refine.py, mkref hand stages)
components.what_we_do: MediaPipe Hands (tracking mode, at most 2 hands) on the colour camera. Stereo depth is projected into that camera. Per frame, MediaPipe's own 3-D hand shape (its world landmarks) is fitted by rotation, translation and clamped scale to 2-D reprojection plus depth residuals (Huber loss, PnP/RANSAC initialisation). Then: handedness fix, greedy linking (Viterbi optional), outlier rejection, gap interpolation, Savitzky-Golay smoothing. hand_refine takes median bone lengths and a Procrustes palm from the best frames, and rebuilds each finger chain by ray-sphere intersection with clipped lengths. mkref parks a weak hand, fills gaps by riding along with the touched object, separates the hands by 4 cm and adds a 10-frame lead-in.
components.closest_prior_art: MediaPipe Hands https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.10214 (opened). Current best hand estimators: HaMeR https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.05251, WiLoR https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12259, HaWoR https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02973 (all opened). AnyTeleop (vision keypoints to robot hand) https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04577 (opened). NVIDIA's egocentric hand module (ViPE + Dyn-HaMR, in the reconstruction README, opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Lifting to metric scale with stereo depth is a good use of the rig. The 2-D estimator is weaker than the HaMeR/WiLoR/HaWoR class that NVIDIA, Do as I Do and RoboWheel use. With no MANO hand mesh, dense contact estimators (HACO, EgoPHI) are unavailable. Bone-length repair is routine mocap cleanup. Behind current research.
components.evidence_it_matters: Hand separation plus lead-in: ep24 0.080 to 0.232. MediaPipe loses the ep18 right hand at f18-22 and the ep24 right hand at f0-16. Viterbi linking was mixed over 18 episodes. The score effect of hand_refine was not isolated (unmeasured).

components.component: 3a. Own meshes: object-frame TSDF fusion (recon_mesh.py, mesh_color.py, make_assets.py)
components.what_we_do: Dense TSDF (signed-distance volume: 4 mm voxels, ±30 cm cube, 1.2 cm truncation) in each object's body frame along our tracked poses. Depth samples that fall on the hands (MediaPipe bone capsules of 3 cm radius plus a forearm), on the table plane (refitted per frame, 1.5 cm band) or within 1.2 cm of other tracked objects clear free space but never vote for a surface. Voxels more than 4 mm below each frame's table plane count as free. Closing is automatic: fill enclosed unknown space, unless the never-observed share exceeds 0.5, then close only near observed surface. Keep the component nearest the origin, Gaussian-smooth, marching cubes, then the kit's budget_mesh (4096 faces). Fused over several public episodes (library v1-v4), coloured from video, with colourless copies for the simulator. Built from public-episode tracks made with the public scans ('A-lite').
components.closest_prior_art: Co-Fusion https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06629 (opened). MaskFusion https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.09194 (opened). BundleSDF https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14158 (opened); it is also NVIDIA's HOI reconstruction module, a two-stage scan followed by an Isaac Sim drop test (README opened). Tzionas & Gall, 3D Object Reconstruction from Hand-Object Interactions, ICCV 2015 https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_iccv_2015/html/Tzionas_3D_Object_Reconstruction_ICCV_2015_paper.html (opened). HOLD https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18448 (opened). SAM 3D, used by Do as I Do, https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16624 (opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Known method, sensibly adapted to egocentric tabletop scenes with hidden undersides. Three adaptations: occluders clear space without voting surface (instead of being dropped), space below the table is free, and the closing heuristic. Fusing recurring objects across episodes exploits the dataset. Not novel: free-space carving and masking are standard TSDF practice. Behind: SoySauceChicken's CD-O is 0.065 cm against our 0.3-0.6 cm, while Guo's 0.313 cm is level with ours. Behind current research on completing unseen regions: we use no shape prior.
components.evidence_it_matters: Registered AUC with our mesh / with the scan: ep41 0.998 / 0.999, ep23 0.997 / 0.999, ep39 0.953 / 0.997, ep21 0.917 / 0.975. Damaged-scan test: 3 mm noise gives 0.825, 5 mm thicker gives 0.608. Board registration flips in 0-25 % of sampling seeds.

components.component: 3b. Mesh fixes for simulation (below_carve, flatten_base.py, library_v3/v4)
components.what_we_do: Two fixes. First, below-table carving. Second, flatten_base: vertices within 8 mm of the lowest point, along the 'up' of our own perceived resting pose, are moved onto one plane 4 mm above it. It is applied by hand, per object and episode: the sweeper from ep18 (library_v3), and the ep24 board edges at standing frames (library_v4, not yet tested on GPU).
components.closest_prior_art: Make It Stand (Prévost et al., SIGGRAPH 2013) https://hal-univ-tlse3.archives-ouvertes.fr/INRIA/hal-00926855v1 (page opened). Atlas3D (self-supporting 3-D via differentiable simulation) https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.18515 (opened). PhyRecon https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16666 (opened). NVIDIA's mesh-to-USD drop test (HOI module README, opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Same principle as Make It Stand and Atlas3D (a shape must be stable under gravity on its support), but a crude heuristic with no optimisation, applied by hand per object. The owner already judged it not robust. The drop-test trigger matches NVIDIA's own drop test.
components.evidence_it_matters: ep18: 0.345 to 0.715 ± 0.240; 5 of 6 rollouts at 0.79-0.84 with SP/MP success; one seed, the largest single gain measured. ep24 with library_v4: not tested.

components.component: 4a. Reference base: mkref + organiser E2S
components.what_we_do: RANSAC table plane in a ring around the objects, gravity frame, support disc, per-object snap to the table, hand gap filling. The organisers' ego_recon_to_sharpa runs unchanged through compatibility shims (pink/pinocchio IK, MANO-to-robot scale 1.2, optional wrist cost). Hand-object contacts are recomputed from the retargeted robot frames (16 probes, 18 mm, minimum run 2, object-motion gate).
components.closest_prior_art: NVIDIA E2S in video_to_data/robotic_grounding (organisers' code). DexPilot / AnyTeleop fingertip retargeting https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04577 (opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Plumbing around the organisers' retargeter. The same as the baseline; nothing new.
components.evidence_it_matters: E2S makes the wrist jump 10-31 cm per frame. Wrist cost 3.0 caps that at ≤ 8 cm, but has no consistent score effect (−0.03, −0.07, +0.21).

components.component: 4b. Contact-anchored retargeting (contact_retarget.py, robot_clearance.py)
components.what_we_do: Per hand and frame, starting from E2S. Each human fingertip (MANO 4/8/12/16/20) within 25 mm of an object becomes a target: projected onto a signed-distance field of that object's collision pieces (the exact convex pieces Newton/MuJoCo builds, 2.5 mm grid), plus a 1 mm margin. Runs shorter than 3 frames are dropped; the rest are smoothed over 5 frames in the object frame. A Levenberg-Marquardt solve (central differences, ≤ 8 iterations) moves the wrist (bounded ±6 cm / ±0.5 rad from E2S) and the 22 finger joints (within limits). Its residuals: distal-link surface point to target (pseudo-Huber); penetration from CPU MuJoCo mj_collision on the scene's own geoms against objects, table and the other hand; prior toward E2S; continuity with the previous frame. Left hand first, then right; frames without contact relax back to E2S; all 67 robot frames rewritten. robot_clearance shifts the wrist out of contacts and smooths the shifts, with clean frames anchored at zero.
components.closest_prior_art: Contact-anchored retargeting + residual RL (DexGEM) https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24093 (opened). EgoCPT (Sharpa, contact optimisation plus force allocation) https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17572 (opened). DexForge https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06331 (opened). C2Dex https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07045 (opened). Morphometric Imitation (Sharpa) https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28660 (opened). DexMachina collision-aware post-processing https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24853 (abstract opened; detail from repo notes). mink collision limits in SPIDER / Do as I Do (repo notes; code not reopened today). Kovar et al., Footskate Cleanup, SCA 2002 https://research.cs.wisc.edu/graphics/Gallery/kovar.vol/Cleanup (opened; analogue of the anchored blending).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Using the training simulator's exact collision model to measure penetration is a real fidelity detail. Most papers approximate it with capsules or a mesh SDF, but Do as I Do's mink + MuJoCo route is the same idea. Behind the 2026 state of the art: per-frame snapping instead of per-segment medoid anchors (C2Dex/DexForge), tip-site rather than pad targets, no wrench-feasibility check (EgoCPT), no handling of which side of a thin object is touched, no palm contacts.
components.evidence_it_matters: Penetration: ep24 frames with a hand > 2 mm inside something 242 to 62 of 275, p95 20.1 to 6.0 mm; ep18 ~77 % to 11 %. Mean of 6 evaluations: ep12 0.725 to 0.790, ep27 0.942 to 0.911, ep18 about 0, ep24 +0.01. Rollout spread shrinks (ep24 ±0.055 to ±0.002-0.018).

components.component: 4c. Rest settling with stable poses (contact_retarget --rest_settle)
components.what_we_do: Per object and frame, an object is 'free' when: its lowest collision point is within 5 cm of the table top; it does not rest on another object; and no fingertip is within 3 cm, unless it is static (< 4 mm and < 2° per frame). Free frames are turned minimally (heading kept, ≤ 15°) onto the nearest stable resting pose, i.e. a convex-hull facet that contains the centre of mass's projection with a 2 mm margin. They are then shifted vertically onto the table, with anchored least-squares smoothing in time.
components.closest_prior_art: trimesh.poses.compute_stable_poses, the classic quasi-static stable-pose computation https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/blob/main/trimesh/poses.py (source opened today). Picasso (non-penetration + physics-constrained sampling) https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08058 (opened). Real-to-Sim for cluttered scenes (contact graph + differentiable simulation) https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12633 (opened). SPIDER stability check and Do as I Do warmup / transition penalty (repo notes). Footskate cleanup (opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: A cheap kinematic rule set driven by our own perception. Published physics-consistent pose refinement uses real simulation or sampling. Ours is quasi-static only and skips objects supported by other objects (pot on rack).
components.evidence_it_matters: CPU, assist off: ep12 cup tip of 23° becomes 0.4 cm / 3.5°; ep27 rack drop 1.05 to 0.03 cm. GPU: ep12 0.740 vs 0.790 without it (−0.05, one seed). It helps only with the flattened sweeper (ep18 0.715).

components.component: 5. Policy (FlashCHORD/FlashSAC + patch_flashchord.py)
components.what_we_do: The organisers' FlashCHORD (Newton / MuJoCo Warp, 4096 worlds). Training uses a virtual object controller: an assist force moves the object along the reference and fades out by about 123M steps. The contact reward is CHORD's contact-wrench term; actions are residuals. FlashSAC, 250M steps per episode, seeds 42/43. Checkpoint sweep at 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8 of training, chosen by sim_vs_ref. Opt-in patches: FC_IMMEDIATE_FIRST_FRAME, where a fraction of late resets start like the evaluation (frame 0, exact fingers, no hold), modelled on NVIDIA's own ReconBody reset; FC_OBJECT_KEYPOINT_SCALE, object keypoints at 15 cm instead of 1 m. Also tested: the primitive-collision hand and a stiffer wrist.
components.closest_prior_art: CHORD https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00033 (opened). FlashSAC https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04539 (opened). DexMachina https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24853 (opened). FlashDexRetarget https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01849 (opened; one policy over many references: 90 % vs 46 % for CHORD at about 1/100 of the compute). ManipTrans https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21860 (opened). DexTrack https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09614 (opened). Gen2Dex https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24392 (opened). OATH https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14379 (opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Both patches are small adaptations (one borrowed from the organisers' humanoid reset, one close to FlashDexRetarget's metric-scale point reward), and neither beat noise. Behind current research: per-episode training from scratch, no multi-reference training, no backward curriculum, no one-sided fingertip reward. Clearly behind Zihao Guo's 19 of 20 successes (SP-SR 0.95).
components.evidence_it_matters: Start fix: no effect (ep18 0.351 vs 0.345). Keypoint scale: ep18 0.381 ± 0.012 vs 0.319-0.361, within noise. Stiffer wrist worse (ep18 0.193 vs 0.381). Primitive hand +0.03 on ep18, −0.015 on ep24. Every ep24 variant ends at 0.31-0.32: the stand-up is not learned.

components.component: 6. Selection and QA (qa.py, auto_ep.sh, score_registered.py, CPU probes)
components.what_we_do: Reference gates: wrist IK p95 and wrist step. Policy verdict: the evaluator rollout scored with the kit's metric functions against our own reference, versus the 'nothing moves' floor (harmful / weak / ok). auto_ep trains ranked reference variants with retries and keeps the best by sim_vs_ref; 6 repeat evaluations. CPU probes with FlashCHORD's exact package versions: drop tests with the assist off, and per-frame pop tests (one physics step after a reset). score_registered reproduces the kit's mesh-to-scan registration locally, with the public scans as a stand-in; diagnostic only, after inference.
components.closest_prior_art: Success measured against the reference in SPIDER https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.09484 and ManipTrans https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21860 (both abstracts opened; metric details from repo notes). NVIDIA's mesh-to-USD drop test (README opened). DexAgent's verifiers https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35318 (opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Scoring against the reference is the field's standard. Our discipline is better than typical: the object reference is fixed across variants, so it is a fair yardstick, and we checked that this ground-truth-free score agrees with the true score. Probably ahead of most entrants in measurement rigour (unverified).
components.evidence_it_matters: sim_vs_ref correlates 0.98 with the mocap score (8 rollouts of one policy). It ranked base vs retargeting like the true score on all 4 episodes (one tie). Spread between evaluations of one policy: ±0.01-0.10 (ep18 kfi ±0.24). CPU probes found 4 root causes before any GPU spend.

components.component: 7. Ops (ops/vast.sh, ops/box/*, auto_ep.sh)
components.what_we_do: Vast.ai API calls via curl, environment snapshot restore (~2 min), on-start job runner. Stall watchdog: if no output file changes and GPU use stays below 10 % for 30 min, save then self-destroy. Periodic pushes to a private Hugging Face store with a size cap. Remote commands over HTTPS through a Cloudflare tunnel instead of SSH. One-command episode pipeline.
components.closest_prior_art: SkyPilot autostop / autodown https://docs.skypilot.co/en/stable/reference/auto-stop.html (search result only, not opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: Solid MLOps, not new. Relevant only to cost and to the Industry Innovation story.
components.evidence_it_matters: No score effect. Overnight: $49.76 for 13 boxes; about 3.3 h per 250M-step training at ~21k steps/s.

components.component: 8. Interaction-aware meshes (in progress, owner's idea)
components.what_we_do: Planned, not in the pipeline (census scripts only, in the scratchpad). Shape the meshes from four constraints: objects must not overlap when they are in the same place at the same time (the ep24 boards overlap 13.5 cm³ at the assembled pose, so the slots should be carved); the volume the hands sweep through is empty; resting objects touch the table with a flat patch; fingertip contacts lie on the surface.
components.closest_prior_art: Vysics ('physible' geometry inferred from contact-rich object motion, fused with BundleSDF's visible geometry) https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.18719 (opened). Picasso https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08058 (opened). Real-to-Sim for cluttered scenes https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12633 (opened). Tzionas & Gall ICCV 2015 (opened). HOLD https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18448 (opened). HOMAN (hand-object contact and penetration losses) https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07044 (opened). NeuralFeels (touch as surface evidence) https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13469 (opened). Swept volume as free-space evidence https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21410 (opened). PhyRecon https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16666 (opened).
components.what_is_genuinely_different: A hypothesis; nothing is built or measured. Searches today: 'jointly reconstruct object shapes non-penetration contact swept volume free space carving', 'physically plausible reconstruction stability differentiable simulation', 'underside support plane shape completion stability'. No paper found that builds rigid object meshes from egocentric stereo across episodes by combining all four constraints, with hand evidence from vision (no touch sensors). Each ingredient exists. Vysics is the closest single precedent and must be cited; Picasso is the closest multi-object one.
components.evidence_it_matters: None yet. The defects that motivate it are measured: the rounded sweeper underside (fixing it took ep18 from 0.345 to 0.715) and the missing ep24 slots (13.5 cm³ overlap).

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Replace hand-applied flatten_base with 'physible geometry' (Vysics-style). Edit only never-observed voxels of each object's signed-distance volume so that: at every rest frame the support polygon under our perceived pose contains the centre of mass and touches the table; objects never overlap when co-located; the volume the hands sweep through stays empty.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: One automatic rule instead of per-object, per-episode patches. It would also cover the ep24 slots and standing edges, and the eval twins (19, 25, 30, 38) whose undersides or edges the cameras never see.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On the 12 two-object public episodes: (i) the share of objects that pass the assist-off drop test at every rest segment rises to ≥ 90 %; (ii) no episode's registered AUC with our meshes drops by more than 0.01. Falsified if either fails.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-4 CPU days, no GPU. Risk: tracking error turns into shape error (we fit the mesh to our own poses); thin boards; enforcing non-overlap at co-located frames may carve real material if poses are off by 1-2 cm.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Vysics (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.18719); Picasso (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08058); Make It Stand (SIGGRAPH 2013)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Complete unseen regions with a generative shape prior: SAM 3D Objects or a similar image-to-3D model, conditioned on and fused with our TSDF, instead of TSDF closing heuristics.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The CD-O gap (0.3-0.6 cm vs 0.065) is concentrated in regions the cameras never see. Do as I Do and RoboWheel already use generated meshes for exactly this.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Per object, Chamfer distance to the public scan on hidden regions (scan used for diagnostics only), plus registered AUC on public episodes. Falsified unless it beats TSDF + flatten on ≥ 8 of 11 objects with no new flips.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 1-2 days, a few GPU hours. Risks: model licence vs the Apache-2.0 release rule; scale and frame alignment to the canonical frame; invented details that flip the scorer's registration.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: SAM 3D (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16624); Do as I Do (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19333)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Train one policy on all 40 perception-derived references (20 public + 20 eval, no ground truth), using FlashDexRetarget's recipe: ADD-like reward on the top-3 surface-point errors, one-sided fingertip reward, an encoder over the next 10 reference frames, per-hand critics.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: FlashDexRetarget reports 90 % success vs 46 % for CHORD at about 1/100 of the compute, on the same hand. Skills learned on public twins (board lift, sweeping) would transfer to eval episodes, and fewer seeds would be needed to fight rollout noise.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Same GPU budget; mean of 6 evaluations on ep12, ep18, ep24 and ep27. Falsified if the mean is not ≥ 0.03 above the best per-episode policies, or if ep24 stays ≤ 0.35.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-4 days to port plus ~$20-40 GPU. High integration risk: the result must still be a FlashCHORD checkpoint the official evaluator accepts.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: FlashDexRetarget (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01849)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Make the hard segments physically feasible first: SPIDER / Do as I Do sampling MPC in MuJoCo Warp with the Sharpa model, or OmniHOI-style CMA-ES over per-keyframe offsets. Then use the result as the RL reference or as a source of reset states.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Every reference fix left ep24 at about 0.32: the stand-up is never learned. A sampler that finds a working contact sequence removes the need for RL to discover it.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: With no policy at all, the MPC must stand ep24 board 1 within 3 cm / 30° of the reference by f120 in at least 1 of 5 seeds. If it cannot, falsified, and no GPU training is spent on it.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 2-4 days plus GPU hours. Risks: MuJoCo Warp vs Newton dynamics mismatch; the MPC needs the missing slots and edges first (idea 1).
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: SPIDER (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.09484); Do as I Do (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19333); OmniHOI (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10855)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Plan robot motion from the object, not the human fingers. Per segment from tools/manip_segments.py, place a grasp synthesised on our mesh (BODex/Dexonomy, or antipodal points), carry it rigidly along the perceived object trajectory, and turn slides into pushing contacts. The policy is still trained by RL on this reference.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The scorer sees only the objects. MediaPipe loses hands during fast motion and occlusion. Contact-invariant optimisation (Mordatch 2012) shows hand motion can be synthesised from object goals alone.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep24 and ep18 policies trained on primitive references, mean of 6 evaluations. Falsified unless they beat the contact-retargeted policies by ≥ 0.05.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 3-5 days. Risks: transitions between segments and two-hand coordination; grasps that are kinematically fine but cannot apply enough force.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Mordatch, Popović & Todorov, Contact-Invariant Optimization for Hand Manipulation, SCA 2012 (search result only; publisher page returned 403); BODex (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16490); Dexonomy (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.18829)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Backward curriculum with a cache of resets that pass the pop test: start training near the end of each hard segment and move the start earlier as success grows.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The ep24 stand-up (f100-120) is reached rarely from early resets. Gen2Dex reports 9 of 10 tasks with valid reset states vs 0 of 10 with raw ones.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep24, two seeds, 250M steps each. Falsified if the mean of 6 evaluations is ≤ 0.35.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About one day for a FlashCHORD reset patch plus ~$5. Risk: training starts drift further from the evaluation, which always begins at frame 0; keep a share of frame-0 resets.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Gen2Dex (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24392); Reverse Curriculum Generation (https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.05300); DeepMimic's reference-state initialisation (https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02717)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Clean object tracks the way animators clean footskate. Label each frame per object as resting, hand-carried, pushed or supported by another object. Enforce each mode's constraints exactly (zero velocity at rest, contact with the supporting surface, no sliding) and blend the corrections smoothly into neighbouring frames.
