This extends rest_settle to object-on-object support and to early drift.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: Objects float 1-4 cm above the table in our references, and some drift before any hand touches them (ep18 from step 16). RL must absorb these reference errors, and every mode violation is a target it cannot track.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Score the references against mocap on all 20 public episodes (after inference, diagnostic only) and count assist-off drop-test passes. Falsified if neither improves.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 1-2 CPU days. Risk: a mislabelled mode (a held object labelled as resting) would freeze motion that really happened.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Kovar, Schreiner & Gleicher, Footskate Cleanup (SCA 2002, page opened); Picasso (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08058)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Train for lower variance between evaluations: noise on the initial state, small physics randomisation, and checkpoint choice by the mean of N evaluations instead of one.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: One ep18 policy spans 0.179-0.842 over 6 evaluations, and the leaderboard sees one rollout per episode. Halving that spread may be worth more than any reference fix.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: On ep18 and ep12, falsified unless the standard deviation over 6 evaluations halves without lowering the mean.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Low, about $5-10. Risk: a slightly lower best-case score.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Domain randomisation and robust control; our own measured rollout noise

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Estimate physical parameters from perception: mass from reconstructed volume times a category density, plus friction priors, instead of the kit's 0.3 kg placeholder for every object.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: A thin wooden board and a pot are not the same mass. Lift and stand-up difficulty, and stability with the assist off, depend on it. Recent real-to-sim work refines poses and physical properties together.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: CPU replay plus one GPU run of ep24 with board masses from volume. Falsified if the change is within noise.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: Low cost. Rule risk: whether masses are ours to set is an open organiser question. There is no ground truth to validate the masses against.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: Real-to-Sim for cluttered scenes (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12633); PhysTwin (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17973)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: Refine each eval episode's meshes BundleSDF-style: track with the library mesh, re-fuse the mesh along that episode's own tracks, re-track, and repeat. This removes the dependence on library meshes built from public tracks that used the scans.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: A mesh fused along its own tracks cancels a constant tracking bias (a work-log observation) and adapts to the eval capture. It also makes the eval pipeline independent of scan-bootstrapped tracks, which matters for rule compliance and the Innovation narrative.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: Run the pending H2 check (8 public episodes tracked with our meshes) with and without one refinement round. Falsified if registered AUC does not improve or flips appear.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: About one day plus about 1 GPU hour per episode. Risk: drift feedback, where tracking error gets baked into the shape.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: BundleSDF (https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14158); Co-Fusion (https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06629)

out_of_box_ideas.idea: A simpler embodiment for the hard episodes: a floating parallel-jaw gripper per hand, or NVIDIA's primitive-collision Sharpa hands, with gripper retargeting as in RoboWheel and Phantom.
out_of_box_ideas.why_it_could_beat_ours: The scored quantity is the object pose. A pinch on a board edge or sweeper handle is far easier to learn than a five-finger grasp.
out_of_box_ideas.falsification_test: ep24 with a gripper reference, 2 seeds. Falsified unless it beats the Sharpa variants (0.31) by ≥ 0.1.
out_of_box_ideas.cost_and_risk: 3-5 days for a new FlashCHORD embodiment. High rule risk: the FAQ's examples are floating hands and arm-and-hand setups, so ask the organisers first.
out_of_box_ideas.source_or_analogy: RoboWheel (https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02729); Phantom (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00779)
